### Quiz Content

## Question 1

After a doctors visit, when should you fill a new prescription?

A) Only when you run out of your current medications
B) As soon as possible, ideally the same day
C) Whenever you remember, even if it is months later
D) Only if the pharmacy offers a discount

answer: B
explanation: Filling your prescription right away ensures you do not forget and start your treatment on schedule. It also lets the pharmacist check for drug interactions and answer any questions you may have.

## Question 2

What should you do if you have questions about your visit summary or discharge instructions?

A) Ignore them and hope for the best
B) Call your doctors office to clarify before the next appointment
C) Wait until your next visit and ask then
D) Ask a friend to interpret the medical terms

answer: B
explanation: If anything in your visit summary is unclear, call your doctors office soon after the visit. Getting clarification quickly helps you follow your care plan correctly and avoid mistakes with medications or follow-up steps.

## Question 3

Why is it important to schedule your next follow-up visit before leaving the office?

A) It saves you a phone call later and ensures you get an appointment at a good time
B) The office charges less if you schedule ahead of time
C) It is not important; you can call whenever you want
D) The doctor will only see you if you schedule before leaving

answer: A
explanation: Scheduling your follow-up before leaving guarantees you a convenient appointment time and reduces the chance you will forget to book one later. Keeping follow-up appointments is key to managing your health.

## Question 4

What should you do with medical documents like lab orders or referral forms after your visit?

A) Throw them away since everything is electronic now
B) Keep them in a folder or file where you can find them easily
C) Mail them back to your doctors office
D) Post them on the refrigerator as a reminder

answer: B
explanation: Keep important medical documents, lab orders, and referral forms in a designated folder or file. Having them organized and accessible ensures you can follow through with tests and specialist appointments without delay.

## Question 5

If your doctor ordered lab work, when should you expect to hear about the results?

A) The lab calls you the same day
B) Doctors usually contact patients within a few days to a week with results
C) You never hear back unless something is wrong
D) Results are mailed to your home address in one month

answer: B
explanation: Most doctors offices contact patients with lab results within a few days to a week. If you have not heard back after a week, call the office. No news is not always good news, so it is best to follow up.

## antibiotic-stewardship

| lessonId  | "antibiotic-stewardship"      |
| passScore | 70                            |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Antibiotics are effective against which type of infection?

A) Most common colds caused by viruses
B) Bacterial infections when appropriately prescribed
C) All sore throats regardless of cause
D) Seasonal allergies

answer: B
explanation: Antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses or allergies. Most colds and many sore throats are viral; only specific bacterial causes warrant antibiotics after proper evaluation.

## Question 2

Why is stopping antibiotics early a concern?

A) It always causes instant resistance in the patient
B) It may not fully clear the infection and can select harder-to-treat bacteria
C) It makes the medicine work better later
D) It has no effect on treatment outcomes

answer: B
explanation: Incomplete treatment can leave surviving bacteria and contribute to resistance. It does not instantly make you permanently resistant, does not improve future efficacy, and clearly affects outcomes.

## Question 3

What is a serious side effect linked to antibiotic use?

A) C. difficile colitis
B) Improved vision
C) Permanent immunity to all infections
D) Lower cholesterol

answer: A
explanation: Antibiotics can disrupt gut flora and allow C. diff overgrowth, causing severe diarrhea. They do not improve vision, grant broad immunity, or lower cholesterol.

## Question 4

What should you do with leftover antibiotic pills?

A) Save them for the next cold
B) Share with a family member with similar symptoms
C) Dispose of them safely per pharmacy guidance — do not self-treat later
D) Take double dose to finish the bottle faster

answer: C
explanation: Leftover antibiotics may be the wrong drug, dose, or duration for a new illness. Saving, sharing, or doubling doses without medical direction is unsafe.

## Question 5

Why does the CDC emphasize antibiotic stewardship?

A) Antibiotics are no longer used in hospitals
B) Resistant bacteria make infections harder and sometimes impossible to treat
C) Viruses are becoming resistant to antibiotics
D) Stewardship means avoiding all medical care

answer: B
explanation: Resistance limits treatment options for serious bacterial infections. Antibiotics remain essential in hospitals; viruses do not become antibiotic-resistant — bacteria do; stewardship promotes appropriate use, not avoiding care.

## anxiety-and-panic

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is the difference between normal anxiety and an anxiety disorder?

A) There is no difference
B) Normal anxiety is temporary and proportional to a situation; an anxiety disorder involves excessive, persistent worry that interferes with daily life
C) Anxiety disorders are caused by bad parenting
D) Normal anxiety only happens at night

answer: B
explanation: Everyone feels anxious sometimes. Normal anxiety is a natural response to stress and goes away when the situation passes. An anxiety disorder involves intense, excessive worry that lasts for months and makes it hard to work, sleep, or socialize.

## Question 2

What is a panic attack?

A) A sudden, intense wave of fear that triggers severe physical reactions even when there is no real danger
B) A mild feeling of nervousness before a test
C) A chronic state of worry that lasts all day
D) A type of allergic reaction

answer: A
explanation: Panic attacks come on suddenly and can include racing heart, chest pain, sweating, shaking, shortness of breath, and a feeling of losing control. Many people mistake panic attacks for heart attacks. They usually peak within 10 minutes.

## Question 3

Which of the following is a common symptom of generalized anxiety disorder?

A) Feeling perfectly calm in all situations
B) Excessive worry about everyday things like work, health, or family that is hard to control
C) Complete inability to feel fear
D) Sudden bursts of uncontrollable laughter

answer: B
explanation: People with generalized anxiety disorder worry excessively about a variety of everyday concerns. The worry is out of proportion to the situation, difficult to control, and often accompanied by restlessness, fatigue, muscle tension, and trouble sleeping.

## Question 4

What breathing technique can help during a moment of acute anxiety?

A) Holding your breath for as long as possible
B) Taking fast, shallow breaths
C) Slow, deep breathing where you breathe in for 4 counts, hold for 4, and breathe out for 4
D) Breathing only through your mouth rapidly

answer: C
explanation: Slow, deep breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system, which helps calm the bodys stress response. Box breathing in for 4, hold for 4, out for 4 is a simple technique that can reduce anxiety symptoms in the moment.

## Question 5

Is anxiety treatable?

A) No, anxiety is a lifelong sentence
B) Yes, anxiety disorders are highly treatable with therapy, medication, or both
C) Yes, but only with medication that has severe side effects
D) No, anxiety can only be managed with alcohol

answer: B
explanation: Anxiety disorders are very treatable. Cognitive behavioral therapy is particularly effective. Many people also benefit from medication. With proper treatment, most people with anxiety disorders can manage their symptoms and live full, productive lives.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which of the following is the most important reason to tell your doctor about all medications you are taking?

A) So the doctor can prescribe more of the same medication
B) To avoid dangerous drug interactions between medications
C) To save money on your pharmacy bill
D) So the doctor can contact your pharmacist

answer: B
explanation: Telling your doctor about every medication you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, helps prevent harmful drug interactions. Some medications can cancel each other out or combine to cause serious side effects.

## Question 2

What should you ask your doctor before starting a new medication?

A) What color the pill is
B) Whether similar medications are cheaper in other countries
C) What the medication is for, how to take it, and what side effects to expect
D) How much weight you will lose from taking it

answer: C
explanation: Before starting any new medication, you should understand its purpose, the correct dosage and timing, potential side effects, and any food or activity restrictions. This helps you take the medication safely and effectively.

## Question 3

What does the term "generic" mean when referring to medication?

A) A medication that is less effective than the brand name
B) A medication that does not require a prescription
C) A copy of a brand-name drug that has the same active ingredients
D) A medication that is only available in liquid form

answer: C
explanation: Generic medications contain the same active ingredients as brand-name drugs and must meet the same FDA standards for safety and effectiveness. They are usually much cheaper than brand-name versions.

## Question 4

If you forget to take a dose of your medication, what is the safest approach?

A) Take a double dose at the next scheduled time
B) Skip the missed dose and never take it again
C) Check the medication label or ask your pharmacist what to do
D) Crush the pill and mix it with food

answer: C
explanation: Instructions for missed doses vary by medication. Some should be taken as soon as you remember, while others should be skipped if close to the next dose. Always check the label or ask your pharmacist to be safe.

## Question 5

Why is it important to keep an updated list of your medications with you at all times?

A) So you can show your insurance company
B) Emergency responders need to know what medications you take
C) To prove you are following your doctors orders
D) So you can compare prices at different pharmacies

answer: B
explanation: In an emergency, paramedics and emergency room doctors need to know exactly what medications you are taking to make safe treatment decisions. An updated list can prevent dangerous errors.

## asthma-basics

> Source file: `content/quizzes/en/asthma-basics.mdx`

| passScore | 70                   |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is asthma?

A) A condition where the lungs fill with fluid
B) A chronic condition where airways become inflamed and narrow, making it hard to breathe
C) A temporary infection of the throat
D) A type of allergic reaction to food

answer: B
explanation: Asthma is a chronic lung condition. The airways become swollen, produce extra mucus, and the muscles around them tighten. This narrows the airways and causes wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath.

## Question 2

What is a common trigger for asthma symptoms?

A) Drinking cold water
B) Exercise, allergies, cold air, or respiratory infections
C) Eating too much protein
D) Exposure to sunlight

answer: B
explanation: Asthma triggers vary by person but commonly include pollen, dust mites, pet dander, mold, cold air, exercise, smoke, and colds or flu. Identifying and avoiding your personal triggers is a key part of asthma management.

## Question 3

What is the difference between a rescue inhaler and a controller inhaler?

A) There is no difference
B) Rescue inhalers are used daily; controller inhalers are used only in emergencies
C) Rescue inhalers provide quick relief during an asthma attack; controller inhalers reduce airway inflammation over time
D) Controller inhalers are only for children

answer: C
explanation: Rescue inhalers contain quick-acting medication that relaxes airway muscles during an attack, providing fast relief. Controller inhalers contain anti-inflammatory medication taken daily to prevent symptoms. Both play important roles in asthma management.

## Question 4

What should you do if your rescue inhaler does not relieve asthma symptoms?

A) Wait another hour and try again
B) Take a hot shower to open your airways
C) Seek emergency medical help immediately
D) Drink a large amount of water

answer: C
explanation: If your rescue inhaler does not work or symptoms get worse, seek emergency care right away. Severe asthma attacks can be life-threatening. Signs of a severe attack include gasping for air, inability to speak full sentences, and blue lips or fingernails.

## Question 5

Can asthma be cured?

A) Yes, with the right medication
B) No, asthma is a chronic condition that can be managed but not cured
C) Yes, but only with surgery
D) Yes, it goes away on its own after childhood

answer: B
explanation: Asthma is a chronic condition with no cure, but it can be effectively managed. With proper treatment, an asthma action plan, and avoiding triggers, most people with asthma can live active, full lives without frequent symptoms.

## Question 1

What is the most important thing to bring to your doctors appointment?

A) A snack and a bottle of water
B) Your ID, insurance card, and a list of your current medications
C) A friend who can drive you home
D) Your favorite book to read in the waiting room

answer: B
explanation: Bringing your ID and insurance card is essential for check-in. A current medication list including doses and frequencies helps your doctor make safe and informed decisions about your care.

## Question 2

Why should you write down your questions before a doctors visit?

A) So you can impress your doctor with how prepared you are
B) To avoid forgetting important concerns during the appointment
C) Because the receptionist collects your questions at check-in
D) So the doctor does not have to talk to you

answer: B
explanation: Doctor visits are often short and can feel overwhelming. Writing down your questions beforehand ensures you cover everything that matters to you, even if you feel nervous or rushed during the appointment.

## Question 3

What should you do if you have new symptoms but your appointment is weeks away?

A) Wait until the appointment and then mention them
B) Call your doctors office to ask if you should come in sooner
C) Go to the emergency room for any new symptom
D) Try to treat the symptoms yourself without medical advice

answer: B
explanation: If new symptoms develop before your scheduled appointment, call your doctors office. They can advise whether you need to be seen sooner, speak with a nurse, or if it is safe to wait. Some symptoms need prompt attention.

## Question 4

How far in advance should you arrive for a typical doctors appointment?

A) 2 to 3 hours early
B) Exactly at the appointment time, not earlier
C) 10 to 15 minutes early to complete paperwork
D) Whenever you want, as long as you arrive before the office closes

answer: C
explanation: Arriving 10 to 15 minutes early gives you time to check in, update your insurance information, and complete any necessary forms. This helps the appointment start on time and reduces stress.

## Question 5

What is a "visit summary" and why is it important?

A) A summary of what you watched on TV in the waiting room
B) A document your doctor gives you that explains the visit, any new medications, and follow-up steps
C) A bill for the appointment
D) A summary your friend writes about your symptoms

answer: B
explanation: A visit summary is a document that outlines what was discussed during your appointment, including diagnoses, medication changes, and follow-up instructions. Reviewing it helps ensure you understand and remember your care plan.

## blood-basics

| passScore | 70                  |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What are the main components of blood?

A) Water, salt, and sugar
B) Red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma
C) Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen
D) Vitamins, minerals, and protein

answer: B
explanation: Blood is made of four main components. Red blood cells carry oxygen, white blood cells fight infection, platelets help with clotting, and plasma is the liquid that carries them all. Each plays a vital role in keeping you healthy.

## Question 2

What is the main function of red blood cells?

A) Fighting infections
B) Carrying oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body
C) Helping blood clot after an injury
D) Digesting food in the stomach

answer: B
explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, a protein that picks up oxygen in your lungs and delivers it to tissues throughout your body. Low red blood cell counts can cause fatigue and weakness, a condition called anemia.

## Question 3

What do white blood cells do?

A) Help you breathe
B) Carry nutrients to your organs
C) Fight infections and protect against illness
D) Control your body temperature

answer: C
explanation: White blood cells are part of your immune system. They identify and attack germs like bacteria and viruses. A high white blood cell count can indicate your body is fighting an infection.

## Question 4

What is the role of platelets in the blood?

A) Carrying oxygen to the brain
B) Fighting viruses
C) Helping blood clot to stop bleeding
D) Transporting hormones

answer: C
explanation: Platelets are tiny cell fragments that clump together at the site of an injury to form a plug and stop bleeding. Without enough platelets, even small cuts can bleed excessively.

## Question 5

What is plasma?

A) The solid part of blood
B) The liquid part of blood that carries cells, nutrients, and waste
C) A type of white blood cell
D) A protein that helps with digestion

answer: B
explanation: Plasma is the liquid portion of blood, making up about 55 percent of total blood volume. It carries blood cells, nutrients, hormones, and waste products throughout the body. Plasma is mostly water but contains important proteins and electrolytes.

## Question 1

According to the MyPlate model, what portions of your plate should be filled with fruits and vegetables?

A) One quarter
B) About half of the plate
C) The entire plate
D) A small corner of the plate

answer: B
explanation: The MyPlate model recommends filling half your plate with fruits and vegetables. These foods are rich in vitamins, minerals, and fiber while being low in calories. Eating a variety of colorful produce ensures you get a range of nutrients.

## Question 2

What type of grains should make up at least half of the grains you eat?

A) Refined white grains like white bread and white rice
B) Whole grains like whole wheat, brown rice, oats, and quinoa
C) Enriched grains only
D) Grain-based desserts like cookies and cake

answer: B
explanation: Whole grains contain the entire grain kernel, providing more fiber, protein, vitamins, and minerals than refined grains. Fiber helps with digestion, keeps you full longer, and can lower cholesterol and blood sugar levels.

## Question 3

What is a healthy source of protein to include on your plate?

A) Fried chicken and bacon
B) Lean meat, poultry, fish, beans, eggs, nuts, and tofu
C) Processed lunch meats
D) Foods fried in oil

answer: B
explanation: Healthy protein sources include lean meats, fish, poultry, eggs, beans, lentils, tofu, nuts, and seeds. These provide essential amino acids without excess saturated fat. Aim for a variety of protein sources throughout the week.

## Question 4

What type of fat is considered heart-healthy?

A) Saturated fats found in butter and red meat
B) Trans fats found in many processed snacks
C) Unsaturated fats found in olive oil, avocados, nuts, and fish
D) All fats are equally healthy

answer: C
explanation: Unsaturated fats, including monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats, can help improve cholesterol levels and reduce heart disease risk. Sources include olive oil, avocados, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish like salmon. Limit saturated and avoid trans fats.

## Question 5

What should you drink with a balanced meal for the healthiest choice?

A) Sugary soda or sweetened tea
B) Water or unsweetened beverages
C) Energy drinks
D) Fruit punch with added sugar

answer: B
explanation: Water is the healthiest choice to accompany any meal. It hydrates without adding calories or sugar. Sugary drinks are a major source of added sugar and empty calories. Unsweetened tea or milk are also good options.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which of the following is an essential item for a basic first aid kit?

A) A sewing kit
B) Adhesive bandages in assorted sizes
C) A bottle of soda
D) A magazine

answer: B
explanation: Adhesive bandages are one of the most basic and essential first aid items. A well-stocked kit should include various sizes for cuts, scrapes, and blisters. They protect wounds from dirt and bacteria while they heal.

## Question 2

What is the purpose of including antiseptic wipes in a first aid kit?

A) To clean your hands before eating
B) To clean the skin around a wound to prevent infection
C) To wipe up spilled liquids
D) To remove makeup

answer: B
explanation: Antiseptic wipes kill germs on the skin around a wound, reducing the risk of infection. Clean the wound gently before applying a bandage. Do not use alcohol directly inside deep wounds, as it can damage tissue.

## Question 3

Why should you include a CPR face mask or shield in your first aid kit?

A) To protect yourself from the sun
B) To safely perform rescue breaths without direct mouth-to-mouth contact
C) To cover your face during cold weather
D) To filter dust from the air

answer: B
explanation: A CPR face mask or shield creates a barrier when giving rescue breaths, reducing the risk of disease transmission. It is a small, inexpensive item that makes bystanders more willing to perform CPR in an emergency.

## Question 4

How often should you check and restock your first aid kit?

A) Once every 10 years
B) Every few months to replace expired items and restock used supplies
C) Never, once it is stocked it lasts forever
D) Only after using it for a major emergency

answer: B
explanation: Check your first aid kit every few months. Replace expired medications, restock used bandages and wipes, and make sure the flashlight batteries work. A kit that is out of date or missing supplies is not helpful in an emergency.

## Question 5

Where is the best place to store a first aid kit in your home?

A) In a locked safe that only adults can open
B) In an easily accessible location that everyone in the household knows about
C) In the garage behind boxes
D) In a high cabinet that requires a step stool to reach

answer: B
explanation: Your first aid kit should be easy to reach in an emergency. Place it in a central, accessible location and make sure all household members know where it is. Avoid locking it, as seconds matter during an injury.

## cancer-screening-basics

| passScore | 70                        |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Main purpose of cancer screening?

A) Diagnose every symptom
B) Find early signs before symptoms
C) Replace treatment
D) Guarantee no cancer ever

answer: B
explanation: Screening tests look for early cancer or precancerous changes before you feel sick. They are not the same as diagnosing every symptom — they are preventive tools for people at recommended ages and risk levels.

## Question 2

Typical starting age for colon screening in U.S. guidelines?

A) 18
B) 45
C) 70
D) Only if symptoms

answer: B
explanation: U.S. guidelines now recommend colorectal cancer screening starting at age 45 for average-risk adults. Earlier screening may be needed with family history or certain conditions. Age 18 or 70 alone are not the standard start ages.

## Question 3

Why is family history important?

A) It never changes recommendations
B) It can lead to earlier or more frequent screening
C) Doctors already know it
D) Only matters for children

answer: B
explanation: A parent or sibling with certain cancers can raise your risk. Doctors may recommend starting mammograms, colonoscopy, or other tests earlier or repeating them more often. They cannot assume your history without you sharing it.

## Question 4

What if a screening result is abnormal?

A) Ignore it
B) Ask what it means and next steps
C) Stop all future screening
D) Self-treat

answer: B
explanation: An abnormal result does not always mean cancer, but it needs follow-up. Ask what the finding means, what test comes next, and how soon. Ignoring results or stopping all future screening is unsafe.

## Question 5

Can screening miss cancer?

A) No — it is 100% accurate
B) Yes — report new symptoms even after normal results
C) Only in young people
D) Only for skin cancer

answer: B
explanation: No screening test catches every cancer. False negatives happen. If you develop new symptoms — bleeding, lumps, persistent pain — report them even if a recent screen was normal.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

At what age should most women begin getting mammograms to screen for breast cancer?

A) Age 30
B) Age 40 or as recommended by their doctor based on risk factors
C) Age 60
D) Age 21

answer: B
explanation: Most guidelines recommend women start regular mammograms at age 40. Women with a family history of breast cancer may need to start earlier. Mammograms can detect breast cancer years before a lump can be felt.

## Question 2

What is a colonoscopy used to screen for?

A) Stomach ulcers
B) Colon cancer and precancerous polyps
C) Kidney stones
D) Food allergies

answer: B
explanation: A colonoscopy allows doctors to examine the entire colon for abnormal growths called polyps. Removing these polyps can prevent colon cancer from developing. Screening usually begins at age 45 for average-risk adults.

## Question 3

What does a Pap smear screen for?

A) Ovarian cancer
B) Cervical cancer and precancerous changes in the cervix
C) Urinary tract infections
D) Thyroid problems

answer: B
explanation: A Pap smear collects cells from the cervix to look for abnormal changes that could lead to cervical cancer. Regular screening has dramatically reduced cervical cancer rates. Women typically start screening at age 21.

## Question 4

What is the PSA test used for?

A) Screening for prostate cancer in men
B) Testing for lung function
C) Diagnosing diabetes
D) Checking liver health

answer: A
explanation: The PSA blood test measures prostate-specific antigen, a protein produced by the prostate gland. High levels may indicate prostate cancer, though other conditions can also raise PSA. Men should discuss screening with their doctor starting around age 50.

## Question 5

Why are regular blood pressure screenings important as you age?

A) Blood pressure only matters if you have symptoms
B) High blood pressure often has no symptoms but can cause serious damage to your heart and arteries
C) Blood pressure screenings are only needed for athletes
D) Your blood pressure stays the same throughout your life

answer: B
explanation: High blood pressure is called the silent killer because it usually has no symptoms. Over time, it damages blood vessels and increases the risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney disease. Regular screening is the only way to know your levels.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is a complete blood count or CBC test used for?

A) To measure how fast you can run
B) To check your overall health and detect disorders like anemia or infection
C) To see if your bones are broken
D) To test your eyesight

answer: B
explanation: A CBC measures red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, and platelets. It is a common screening test that can help detect anemia, infection, inflammation, and other blood disorders.

## Question 2

What does a blood pressure reading measure?

A) The speed of blood flow through your veins
B) The force of blood against the walls of your arteries when your heart beats and rests
C) The amount of sugar in your blood
D) How much oxygen is in your lungs

answer: B
explanation: Blood pressure has two numbers: systolic (pressure when the heart beats) and diastolic (pressure when the heart rests between beats). High blood pressure over time can damage your heart and arteries.

## Question 3

What is a cholesterol test also known as?

A) A stress test
B) A lipid panel or lipid profile
C) A glucose tolerance test
D) A thyroid panel

answer: B
explanation: A lipid panel measures total cholesterol, LDL (bad cholesterol), HDL (good cholesterol), and triglycerides. It helps assess your risk for heart disease and stroke.

## Question 4

What is the purpose of a urinalysis?

A) To test how much water you drink
B) To detect kidney problems, urinary tract infections, and other health conditions
C) To measure your lung capacity
D) To check your reflexes

answer: B
explanation: A urinalysis examines the color, concentration, and content of your urine. It can detect kidney disease, urinary tract infections, diabetes, and other conditions. It is a simple, non-invasive test.

## Question 5

What is a fasting blood glucose test used for?

A) To measure your blood sugar after eating a large meal
B) To screen for diabetes and prediabetes after not eating for at least 8 hours
C) To test your iron levels
D) To check your kidney function

answer: B
explanation: A fasting blood glucose test measures your blood sugar after an overnight fast. Normal levels are typically below 100 mg/dL. Higher levels may indicate prediabetes or diabetes and require follow-up testing.

| passScore | 70                    |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which factor is the leading preventable cause of COPD?

A) Cigarette smoking and long-term lung irritant exposure
B) Drinking water daily
C) Seasonal pollen only
D) One episode of childhood asthma

answer: A
explanation: Tobacco smoke is the dominant COPD risk factor; occupational exposures also matter. Water intake, pollen alone, and resolved childhood asthma do not explain typical COPD pathogenesis.

## Question 2

How does asthma airflow limitation typically differ from COPD?

A) Asthma obstruction is often largely reversible with bronchodilators
B) Asthma never causes wheezing
C) COPD always fully reverses with one dose of albuterol
D) Only asthma is diagnosed with spirometry

answer: A
explanation: Asthma features reversible bronchospasm; wheezing is common. COPD has fixed or partially reversible obstruction — not full reversal with one rescue dose. Spirometry helps both conditions.

## Question 3

Which symptoms suggest an asthma attack rather than stable COPD alone?

A) Sudden wheeze and chest tightness after a known trigger
B) Gradual cough over 20 years in a heavy smoker only
C) Slow nail growth over months
D) Chronic knee arthritis

answer: A
explanation: Acute trigger-linked wheeze fits asthma exacerbation. Decades-long smoker's cough fits COPD; nail growth and knee arthritis are unrelated respiratory patterns.

## Question 4

Why is correct inhaler technique important?

A) Poor technique delivers less medicine to the lungs
B) Technique only matters for oral pills
C) Any spray direction works equally
D) Inhalers are decorative only

answer: A
explanation: Deposition in lungs depends on coordination and device use. Technique matters greatly for inhalers, not pills; spray direction and device mechanics affect dose; inhalers are active drug delivery.

## Question 5

When should you seek emergency care for breathing symptoms?

A) Severe breathlessness, blue lips, or inability to speak full sentences
B) Mild cough once in winter only
C) Sneezing from allergies without breathing trouble
D) After normal exercise in healthy young athletes only

answer: A
explanation: Severe respiratory distress with hypoxia signs is emergent. Isolated mild seasonal cough, allergic sneeze without dyspnea, and normal post-exercise breathing in healthy people are lower concern.

| passScore | 70                            |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Why can grapefruit juice be problematic with certain medicines?

A) It always makes medicines work faster safely
B) It can inhibit enzymes and raise drug blood levels
C) It only affects vitamins, not prescriptions
D) It has no clinical significance

answer: B
explanation: Grapefruit inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, increasing absorption of some drugs to potentially toxic levels. It does not universally speed drugs safely, affects many prescriptions, and has well-documented clinical effects.

## Question 2

Why might levothyroxine be taken on an empty stomach?

A) Food always improves thyroid absorption
B) Food and minerals like calcium can reduce absorption
C) It must always be taken with a high-fat meal
D) Timing never matters for thyroid medicine

answer: B
explanation: Food, calcium, and iron can interfere with levothyroxine absorption, so consistent fasting timing is often recommended. Food does not reliably improve absorption; high-fat meals are not required; timing does matter.

## Question 3

What dietary approach helps people on warfarin?

A) Completely avoid all vitamin K forever
B) Keep vitamin K intake fairly consistent day to day
C) Double leafy greens weekly for health
D) Stop warfarin when eating salad

answer: B
explanation: Warfarin dosing is adjusted to consistent vitamin K intake — sudden large changes matter more than moderate steady amounts. Avoiding all vitamin K is unnecessary; erratic doubling or stopping warfarin around meals is unsafe.

## Question 4

Why limit alcohol with acetaminophen?

A) Alcohol improves liver detoxification of acetaminophen
B) Both can stress the liver and increase injury risk
C) Alcohol has no liver effects
D) Only children are at risk

answer: B
explanation: Alcohol and acetaminophen both burden hepatic pathways; combined use raises liver injury risk. Alcohol does not protect the liver, does have hepatic effects, and adults are also at risk.

## Question 5

What should you do when starting a medicine with food warnings on the label?

A) Ignore the label if you feel fine
B) Follow label directions and ask a pharmacist if unclear
C) Always take every drug with a full meal
D) Only take medicines with grapefruit juice

answer: B
explanation: Labels reflect how food affects that specific drug. Ignoring guidance risks under- or overdosing; not every drug needs food; grapefruit is contraindicated for many medicines, not a universal aid.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What should you do if you do not understand something your doctor says during the appointment?

A) Nod and agree so you do not seem difficult
B) Ask the doctor to explain it in simpler terms
C) Look it up on your phone after the appointment
D) Assume it is not important

answer: B
explanation: It is your right to understand your health. Doctors use medical terms that can be confusing. Asking for clarification helps you make informed decisions about your care. A good doctor will be happy to explain.

## Question 2

Why is it important to be honest with your doctor about your habits like smoking, drinking, or diet?

A) So the doctor can judge your lifestyle choices
B) Because these habits affect your health and treatment options
C) So the information can be shared with your employer
D) It is not important; you can keep these private

answer: B
explanation: Your lifestyle directly affects your health risks and how well treatments will work. Doctors need accurate information to provide the best care. They are bound by privacy laws and are there to help, not judge.

## Question 3

What is a "telehealth" visit?

A) A visit where you talk to your doctor through a phone call or video call
B) A visit where a robot examines you
C) A visit where you send emails to your doctor
D) A visit that happens over the telephone only for emergencies

answer: A
explanation: Telehealth uses technology to connect you with your doctor remotely through phone or video. It is convenient for follow-ups, discussing test results, and managing ongoing conditions when an in-person exam is not needed.

## Question 4

If you see a medical student or a nurse practitioner during your visit, what should you do?

A) Refuse to speak with anyone except the main doctor
B) Ask for a discount because you are seeing a trainee
C) Treat them with respect and answer their questions honestly
D) Leave the appointment immediately

answer: C
explanation: Medical students and nurse practitioners are trained professionals working as part of your care team. They often spend more time with patients and communicate well. You can always ask for the attending doctor if you prefer.

## Question 5

What should you do before leaving your doctors appointment?

A) Ask for a copy of your medical records to take home
B) Make sure you understand the next steps: medications, follow-up visits, and any tests needed
C) Request a second opinion from every doctor in the office
D) Ask the receptionist to call you a taxi

answer: B
explanation: Before leaving, confirm your understanding of the treatment plan, including any new prescriptions, recommended tests, and when to schedule a follow-up. This prevents confusion and helps you follow through with your care.

## generic-vs-brand-drugs

| title     | "Generic vs Brand Quiz"  |
| lessonId  | "generic-vs-brand-drugs" |
| passScore | 70                       |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Generics must have the same:

A) Only color
B) Active ingredient and strength
C) Marketing name
D) Price as brand

answer: B
explanation: Generic drugs must contain the same active ingredient at the same strength as the brand version. Inactive fillers may differ, but the medicine that treats your condition is equivalent for most drugs.

## Question 2

Why might insurance prefer generics?

A) They are less regulated
B) Lower cost with equivalent effectiveness for most drugs
C) They never work
D) They are always brands

answer: B
explanation: Generics cost less because manufacturers do not repeat expensive marketing and trials for the active compound. For most people they work the same — insurance often requires trying generic first.

## Question 3

After switching to generic, you should:

A) Stop all follow-up
B) Report new or worsening side effects to your care team
C) Double the dose
D) Never tell the pharmacist

answer: B
explanation: If you switch to generic and notice new side effects or feel worse, tell your care team. Rarely, sensitivity to fillers matters. Do not silently stop — report changes so they can adjust.

## Question 4

Counterfeit drugs are a risk when:

A) Using licensed pharmacies
B) Buying from unverified online sellers
C) Reading labels
D) Asking questions

answer: B
explanation: Unverified online pharmacies may sell counterfeit or improperly stored drugs. Stick to licensed pharmacies in your country. Low prices from unknown sellers are a red flag, not a bargain.

## Question 5

Bioequivalent means:

A) No active drug
B) Similar blood levels compared to brand within accepted range
C) Only for vitamins
D) Illegal in the U.S.

answer: B
explanation: Bioequivalence means the generic delivers similar blood levels to the brand within FDA-accepted limits. That is why generics are approved — not because they are weaker versions of the same drug.

| passScore | 70                             |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What does glycemic load (GL) add beyond glycemic index (GI)?

A) It ignores portion size entirely
B) It accounts for both food GI and serving size
C) It only measures protein content
D) It replaces blood glucose monitoring

answer: B
explanation: GL multiplies GI by available carbohydrate amount per serving, making portion size part of the estimate. GL does not ignore portions, measure protein, or replace actual glucose monitoring.

## Question 2

Which meal strategy tends to blunt glucose spikes?

A) Carbohydrates alone in large portions
B) Adding fiber, protein, or healthy fat to carbohydrate foods
C) Skipping all vegetables
D) Only drinking sugary beverages

answer: B
explanation: Fiber, protein, and fat slow carbohydrate absorption and moderate post-meal glucose. Large carbs alone, avoiding vegetables, or sugary drinks tend to raise glucose more sharply.

## Question 3

How does the ADA generally view GI/GI-only diets?

A) As the sole treatment for diabetes
B) As one tool within broader healthy eating patterns
C) As unnecessary for everyone with diabetes
D) As a cure for type 1 diabetes

answer: B
explanation: ADA guidance emphasizes overall dietary patterns, medications, and activity — GI/GL can inform choices but are not standalone treatment or cures, and they remain useful for many with diabetes.

## Question 4

Which statement about sugar and type 2 diabetes is most accurate?

A) Eating sugar alone directly causes type 2 diabetes in everyone
B) Type 2 risk involves genetics, weight, activity, and metabolism — not sugar alone
C) Only children develop type 2 diabetes
D) Sugar has no effect on blood glucose

answer: B
explanation: Type 2 diabetes is multifactorial; sugar affects glucose but does not singularly cause the disease in everyone. Adults develop type 2 commonly; sugar clearly affects blood glucose.

## Question 5

Why might two people respond differently to the same high-GI food?

A) GI is identical for every human always
B) Individual metabolism, activity, and medications vary
C) GI only applies to fats
D) Blood glucose never changes after meals

answer: B
explanation: Real-world glucose responses differ by insulin sensitivity, activity, gut microbiome, and meds. GI varies by food, not only fats, and post-meal glucose clearly changes.

| passScore | 70                                  |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which symptom cluster is most typical of stroke?

A) Gradual mild knee pain over weeks
B) Sudden one-sided face droop and slurred speech
C) Itchy eyes from pollen
D) Slow weight gain over years

answer: B
explanation: Stroke symptoms are sudden and neurologic — face, arm, speech changes. Knee pain, allergies, and slow weight change are not stroke hallmarks.

## Question 2

What does the 'T' in FAST stand for regarding stroke?

A) Take a nap first
B) Time — call emergency services immediately
C) Test blood sugar only
D) Travel to clinic next week

answer: B
explanation: FAST emphasizes Time to call 911 because stroke treatments are time-limited. Napping, glucose checks alone, or delayed clinic visits waste critical minutes.

## Question 3

Why call 911 instead of driving yourself for possible heart attack?

A) EMS can start care and route to appropriate hospital faster
B) Driving is always faster than ambulances
C) Hospitals refuse walk-in patients
D) Symptoms always resolve during the drive

answer: A
explanation: Ambulances provide monitoring, aspirin when appropriate, and destination to capable centers. Self-driving risks collapse en route; hospitals accept emergencies; symptoms may worsen, not improve.

## Question 4

Which heart attack symptom may be more subtle in women?

A) Chest discomfort, fatigue, or shortness of breath without classic crushing pain
B) Only hair loss
C) Chronic toenail fungus
D) Seasonal sneezing

answer: A
explanation: Women more often present with atypical chest pressure, fatigue, nausea, or breathlessness. Hair, nail, and allergy symptoms are unrelated to acute MI presentation.

## Question 5

Why note the time symptoms began in suspected stroke?

A) Clinicians use timing to decide eligibility for acute stroke therapies
B) Hospitals charge by the minute only
C) Time is irrelevant to stroke treatment
D) It replaces all brain imaging

answer: A
explanation: IV thrombolysis and thrombectomy windows depend on last known well time. Billing is not the reason; timing is clinically critical; imaging still required.

## how-antidepressants-work

| passScore | 70                              |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

How long do antidepressants often need before full benefit?

A) About 4 to 8 weeks for many people
B) Full effect within 2 hours always
C) At least 2 years before any change
D) Only one dose is ever needed

answer: A
explanation: Most antidepressants require weeks of consistent use. Two hours is unrealistic for full mood effect; two years is not a standard wait for initial response; chronic treatment may continue but not as a single dose.

## Question 2

What do SSRIs primarily affect?

A) Serotonin reuptake in the brain
B) Insulin production in the pancreas
C) Thyroid hormone synthesis only
D) Blood type antigens

answer: A
explanation: SSRIs selectively inhibit serotonin reuptake. They do not primarily act on insulin, thyroid synthesis, or blood group antigens.

## Question 3

Why monitor young adults when starting antidepressants?

A) Risk of worsening mood or suicidal thoughts in some patients early in treatment
B) Antidepressants always cause instant cure without side effects
C) Only children under age 2 take antidepressants
D) Monitoring is required because medicines are placebos only

answer: A
explanation: FDA black box warnings address possible suicidality monitoring early in treatment. Medicines are not instant cure-only drugs, are used in adolescents/adults not toddlers only, and are active drugs not placebos.

## Question 4

What can happen if antidepressants are stopped abruptly?

A) Discontinuation symptoms such as dizziness or flu-like feelings
B) Guaranteed permanent happiness
C) Instant cure of all anxiety forever
D) No possible effects whatsoever

answer: A
explanation: Abrupt stop can cause discontinuation syndrome. Permanent happiness, instant universal anxiety cure, and zero effects are not accurate outcomes of sudden stops.

## Question 5

Why tell all prescribers about antidepressants and supplements?

A) To avoid dangerous interactions like serotonin syndrome
B) So they can discourage all mental health care
C) Supplements never interact with prescriptions
D) Only one doctor ever needs medication information

answer: A
explanation: Combining serotonergic drugs and some supplements risks serotonin syndrome. Providers support care, supplements can interact, and all prescribers need complete med lists.

| lessonId  | "how-statins-work"      |
| passScore | 70                      |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is the primary mechanism of statins?

A) Blocking liver HMG-CoA reductase to reduce cholesterol production
B) Dissolving existing artery plaque overnight
C) Raising HDL by exercising muscles directly
D) Replacing all dietary cholesterol absorption

answer: A
explanation: Statins inhibit hepatic cholesterol synthesis, lowering LDL. They do not instantly dissolve plaque, do not directly exercise muscles, and do not block all dietary cholesterol uptake.

## Question 2

Why should muscle symptoms on a statin be reported?

A) They are always harmless and should be ignored
B) Rare severe muscle injury needs evaluation and possible medication change
C) They mean the statin is curing diabetes
D) Only athletes experience muscle effects

answer: B
explanation: Most muscle complaints are mild, but severe cases need assessment. Symptoms are not always harmless, do not indicate diabetes cure, and affect non-athletes too.

## Question 3

How do ACC/AHA guidelines generally position statins?

A) Only for people already hospitalized
B) For selected high-risk patients alongside lifestyle therapy
C) As replacements for blood pressure medicines
D) Only when LDL is normal

answer: B
explanation: Guidelines recommend statins based on risk and LDL in outpatient prevention too. They complement lifestyle, do not replace BP drugs, and are used when LDL or risk warrants treatment — not only at normal LDL.

## Question 4

What should you do before stopping a prescribed statin due to side effects?

A) Stop immediately without telling anyone
B) Discuss with your clinician for dose change or alternative
C) Double the dose to push through pain
D) Replace with unproven supplements only

answer: B
explanation: Clinicians can adjust therapy safely. Stopping without guidance risks cardiovascular events; doubling dose worsens toxicity; supplements alone lack proven event reduction.

## Question 5

Why might grapefruit be mentioned on some statin labels?

A) It improves statin safety for all statins equally
B) It can raise blood levels of certain statins via enzyme inhibition
C) It has no interaction with any medicines
D) It is required to absorb statins

answer: B
explanation: Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4, increasing exposure for some statins like simvastatin and atorvastatin. It does not universally improve safety, does interact with drugs, and is not required for absorption.

| passScore | 70                     |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Mild dehydration may cause:

A) Only hunger
B) Headache and fatigue
C) Improved athletic performance
D) Lower heart rate always

answer: B
explanation: Mild dehydration often shows up as headache, fatigue, dry mouth, or dark urine before severe illness develops. These symptoms can mimic other conditions, so consider fluid intake when they appear together.

## Question 2

Who may need fluid limits instead of more water?

A) Healthy young athletes only
B) Some people with heart or kidney disease
C) Everyone over 65
D) Only children

answer: B
explanation: People with heart failure, kidney disease, or certain medications may need fluid limits set by their doctor. Drinking extra water without guidance can be harmful for them — not everyone needs the same amount.

## Question 3

A practical hydration check for many people is:

A) Never urinate
B) Pale yellow urine and drinking when thirsty
C) Only drink at meals
D) Avoid all fluids at night

answer: B
explanation: Pale yellow urine and drinking when thirsty are practical signs of adequate hydration for most healthy adults. Clear urine all day or forcing large volumes without need are not better goals for everyone.

## Question 4

Best default drink for daily hydration:

A) Sugary soda
B) Water
C) Energy drinks only
D) Alcohol

answer: B
explanation: Water is the best default drink for daily hydration — no added sugar or calories. Sugary sodas and energy drinks add empty calories. Unsweetened options are fine, but water remains the baseline recommendation.

## Question 5

Severe dehydration requires:

A) Ignoring it
B) Urgent medical evaluation
C) Only extra coffee
D) Skipping all food forever

answer: B
explanation: Severe dehydration — confusion, fainting, no urine for many hours, rapid heartbeat — needs urgent medical care. Home remedies alone are not enough when the body shows signs of significant fluid loss.

| passScore | 70                                  |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is insulin resistance?

A) Cells respond poorly to insulin, requiring more insulin to control glucose
B) The pancreas makes too much insulin only in type 1 diabetes always
C) Complete absence of any insulin from birth
D) A condition cured by one day of fasting

answer: A
explanation: Resistance means reduced cellular response, driving compensatory hyperinsulinemia. Type 1 is insulin deficiency, not resistance-only; absence from birth describes type 1; one-day fasting does not cure metabolic disease.

## Question 2

Which ADA A1c range defines prediabetes?

A) 5.7% to 6.4%
B) Below 4.0%
C) Above 10% only
D) Exactly 8.0% always

answer: A
explanation: Prediabetes A1c is 5.7–6.4%; diabetes is ≥6.5%. Below 4% is unusually low; 10% suggests poorly controlled diabetes, not prediabetes definition; 8% is not the prediabetes band.

## Question 3

What did the Diabetes Prevention Program lifestyle intervention achieve?

A) Roughly 58% reduction in progression to type 2 in high-risk adults
B) 100% cure of all diabetes types
C) No effect compared to usual care
D) Only worked in people under age 12

answer: A
explanation: DPP showed major risk reduction with weight loss and activity in adults. It did not cure all diabetes, clearly beat usual care, and targeted adults at risk, not only children.

## Question 4

Which factor contributes to insulin resistance?

A) Excess visceral fat and physical inactivity
B) Wearing glasses
C) Drinking water daily
D) Seasonal pollen allergies alone

answer: A
explanation: Visceral adiposity and inactivity worsen insulin signaling. Glasses, hydration, and pollen allergies are not established drivers of insulin resistance.

## Question 5

Why screen for prediabetes even without symptoms?

A) Damage can start before symptoms and lifestyle change is most effective early
B) Prediabetes always causes immediate pain
C) Screening is only for hospitalized patients
D) There is no proven way to slow progression

answer: A
explanation: Prediabetes is often silent yet progressive; early intervention works. It is not always painful, screening is outpatient, and DPP proves progression can be slowed.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is heart disease?

A) Any condition that affects the brain
B) A group of conditions that affect the heart and blood vessels, including coronary artery disease
C) An infection of the heart muscle
D) A temporary condition that only affects older adults

answer: B
explanation: Heart disease is an umbrella term for conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels. The most common type is coronary artery disease, where plaque builds up in the arteries supplying blood to the heart. Heart disease is the leading cause of death in the United States.

## Question 2

What is a heart attack?

A) When the heart stops beating completely
B) When blood flow to a part of the heart muscle is blocked, usually by a blood clot
C) When the heart beats too fast temporarily
D) When the lungs stop working

answer: B
explanation: A heart attack occurs when blood flow to the heart is severely reduced or blocked, usually by a clot in a narrowed artery. Without oxygen, heart muscle begins to die. Quick treatment is critical to minimize damage.

## Question 3

Which of the following is a major risk factor for heart disease?

A) Getting enough sleep
B) High blood pressure, high cholesterol, and smoking
C) Eating a balanced diet
D) Regular physical activity

answer: B
explanation: Major risk factors for heart disease include high blood pressure, high cholesterol, smoking, diabetes, obesity, and a family history of heart disease. Many of these can be managed through lifestyle changes and medication.

## Question 4

What lifestyle habit can reduce your risk of heart disease?

A) Smoking cigarettes in moderation
B) Eating a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins
C) Drinking large amounts of alcohol every day
D) Sitting for most of the day without physical activity

answer: B
explanation: A heart-healthy diet includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats while limiting saturated fats, trans fats, sodium, and added sugars. Combined with regular exercise and not smoking, this can significantly reduce heart disease risk.

## Question 5

What does CPR stand for and what is its purpose?

A) Cardiac Pulse Regulation; it regulates the heart rhythm
B) Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation; it keeps blood and oxygen flowing during cardiac arrest
C) Cardio-Pulmonary Recovery; it helps after a heart attack
D) Cardiac Prevention Routine; it prevents heart disease

answer: B
explanation: CPR combines chest compressions and rescue breaths to keep blood and oxygen flowing to the brain and organs when a persons heart has stopped. Bystander CPR can double or triple a cardiac arrest victims chance of survival.

## living-with-hypertension

| passScore | 70                              |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is hypertension?

A) Low blood pressure that causes dizziness
B) Chronically high blood pressure that puts strain on the heart and blood vessels
C) A condition where blood pressure goes up and down rapidly
D) A temporary increase in blood pressure during exercise

answer: B
explanation: Hypertension means your blood pressure stays higher than normal over time. This constant strain damages arteries and increases the risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney disease. It is often called the silent killer because it has no symptoms.

## Question 2

Which lifestyle change can help lower blood pressure?

A) Eating more salty foods
B) Reducing sodium intake, eating a balanced diet, and getting regular exercise
C) Drinking more caffeine
D) Sleeping fewer than 5 hours per night

answer: B
explanation: Reducing salt, eating more fruits and vegetables, maintaining a healthy weight, regular physical activity, limiting alcohol, and managing stress can all help lower blood pressure. Even small changes can make a meaningful difference.

## Question 3

What is a normal blood pressure reading?

A) 140 over 90 or higher
B) 130 over 80 or higher
C) Below 120 over 80
D) 150 over 100

answer: C
explanation: A normal blood pressure reading is below 120 systolic and below 80 diastolic. Readings of 130 over 80 or higher are considered elevated or stage 1 hypertension and should be discussed with your doctor.

## Question 4

Why is medication often needed to manage hypertension?

A) Lifestyle changes never work for lowering blood pressure
B) Some people need medication because lifestyle changes alone are not enough to control their blood pressure
C) Medication cures hypertension permanently
D) Medication is only needed for people over 80

answer: B
explanation: While lifestyle changes are important, many people with hypertension also need medication to reach a safe blood pressure level. Medications work in different ways to relax blood vessels or reduce fluid volume. Never stop blood pressure medication without talking to your doctor.

## Question 5

What should you do if you miss a dose of your blood pressure medication?

A) Take two doses together when you remember
B) Skip the dose and do not worry about it
C) Follow the instructions on your prescription label or ask your pharmacist
D) Stop taking all medications until you see your doctor

answer: C
explanation: If you miss a dose, check your prescription label or call your pharmacist. Some medications should be taken as soon as you remember, while others should be skipped if it is close to the next dose. Never double up unless instructed.

## managing-side-effects

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What should you do first if you experience a side effect from a medication?

A) Immediately stop taking the medication
B) Contact your doctor or pharmacist to discuss the symptom
C) Double your dose to make the side effect go away faster
D) Wait one month to see if it gets worse

answer: B
explanation: Always contact your doctor or pharmacist when you notice a side effect. They can determine if it is normal, adjust your dose, or switch you to a different medication. Stopping medication suddenly can be dangerous.

## Question 2

Which of the following is a common side effect of many medications?

A) Improved vision
B) Increased height
C) Nausea or upset stomach
D) Enhanced memory

answer: C
explanation: Nausea and digestive upset are among the most common side effects across many different medications. Taking medication with food or at a specific time of day can often help reduce these symptoms.

## Question 3

What is the difference between a side effect and an allergic reaction?

A) There is no difference, they are the same thing
B) A side effect is expected and often mild; an allergic reaction involves the immune system and can be serious
C) An allergic reaction only happens with generic drugs
D) Side effects only happen with liquid medications

answer: B
explanation: Side effects are known possible reactions that are usually mild and may go away as your body adjusts. Allergic reactions involve the immune system and can cause hives, swelling, or trouble breathing, which requires immediate medical attention.

## Question 4

What can help reduce medication side effects like dizziness or drowsiness?

A) Taking the medication with grapefruit juice
B) Taking the medication at bedtime if your doctor approves
C) Chewing the medication instead of swallowing it
D) Drinking alcohol to counteract the dizziness

answer: B
explanation: Taking certain medications at bedtime can help manage side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist about the best time to take your medication and whether food or specific timing can help.

## Question 5

If you are taking multiple medications and notice new symptoms, what could be happening?

A) The symptoms are definitely unrelated to your medications
B) You may be experiencing a drug interaction between medications
C) You should take extra vitamins to fix the symptoms
D) Your body is building immunity to the medications

answer: B
explanation: New symptoms when taking multiple medications could signal a drug interaction. Certain combinations can change how medications work in your body. Always report new symptoms to your doctor, especially when starting a new medication.

## managing-stress

| passScore | 70                     |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Chronic stress can affect which body systems?

A) Only mood
B) Sleep, blood pressure, digestion, and more
C) Only athletes
D) Nothing measurable

answer: B
explanation: Long-term stress affects more than mood. It can disrupt sleep, raise blood pressure, upset digestion, and weaken immune response. These physical effects are measurable and worth addressing early.

## Question 2

A helpful daily habit is:

A) Checking news constantly
B) A short walk or breathing break
C) Skipping sleep to finish tasks
D) Isolating from everyone

answer: B
explanation: Brief movement and slow breathing activate the body's calming response without requiring special equipment. Constant news scrolling, sleep deprivation, and isolation tend to worsen stress over time.

## Question 3

When should you seek professional help?

A) Never — stress is always minor
B) When symptoms persist and interfere with daily life
C) Only after hospitalization
D) Only for children

answer: B
explanation: Professional support is appropriate when worry, low mood, or panic lasts weeks and interferes with work, relationships, or self-care. Stress is not always minor — persistent symptoms deserve evaluation.

## Question 4

What is a crisis resource?

A) Ignoring symptoms
B) 24/7 crisis line or emergency services when in danger
C) Only social media advice
D) Stopping all medicine

answer: B
explanation: Crisis lines and emergency services exist for immediate danger, including thoughts of self-harm. They are not a last resort after hospitalization — they are for moments when safety is at risk right now.

## Question 5

Small habits work because:

A) They must be perfect
B) Repeatable actions build recovery over time
C) Stress never returns
D) They replace medical care

answer: B
explanation: Recovery builds through small actions repeated daily — a walk, a breathing pause, a bedtime routine. Perfection is not required, and habits do not replace medical or mental health treatment when needed.

## micronutrient-deficiencies

| lessonId  | "micronutrient-deficiencies"      |
| passScore | 70                                |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which nutrient deficiency is common and often linked to fatigue and anemia?

A) Iron
B) Vitamin C only
C) Sodium
D) Caffeine

answer: A
explanation: Iron deficiency reduces hemoglobin and commonly causes fatigue and anemia. Vitamin C aids absorption but alone does not cause classic anemia pattern; sodium and caffeine are not micronutrient deficiencies in this sense.

## Question 2

Who may need extra attention to vitamin B12 intake?

A) Only infants under six months
B) Older adults and people on strict vegan diets without fortification
C) Everyone should avoid B12 entirely
D) Only competitive athletes

answer: B
explanation: B12 absorption often declines with age; plant-only diets lack B12 unless fortified foods or supplements are used. Infants get B12 from formula or breast milk with adequate maternal intake; avoiding B12 is harmful; athletes are not the primary at-risk group.

## Question 3

Why test before starting high-dose supplements?

A) All deficiencies feel identical
B) Excess of some nutrients can be harmful and symptoms have many causes
C) Blood tests never detect deficiencies
D) Supplements always replace medical care

answer: B
explanation: Testing targets the right deficiency; iron overload and fat-soluble vitamin excess are dangerous. Deficiencies differ symptomatically; blood tests do detect many deficiencies; supplements complement but do not always replace treatment.

## Question 4

Which condition can impair micronutrient absorption?

A) Celiac disease affecting the small intestine
B) Wearing glasses
C) Mild seasonal allergies
D) Regular walking

answer: A
explanation: Celiac damages the small intestine and reduces absorption of iron, folate, and other nutrients. Glasses, mild allergies, and walking do not cause malabsorption syndromes.

## Question 5

Why is folic acid emphasized in pregnancy?

A) It prevents all birth defects of any kind
B) Adequate folate lowers risk of neural tube defects
C) It replaces prenatal care visits
D) It is only needed after delivery

answer: B
explanation: Folic acid before and early in pregnancy reduces neural tube defect risk — it does not prevent all birth defects, does not replace prenatal care, and is needed before conception and early pregnancy, not only postpartum.

## otc-drug-interactions

| passScore | 70                           |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Why is checking active ingredients on multiple OTC labels important?

A) Brands always use different ingredients
B) Duplicate ingredients can exceed safe daily limits
C) Only prescription drugs have active ingredients
D) Labels are optional for adults

answer: B
explanation: Multiple OTC products may share the same active drug (e.g., acetaminophen), pushing total dose past safe limits. Brands often differ, and both prescriptions and OTC products list actives — labels are required, not optional.

## Question 2

Who is especially helpful for screening drug interactions?

A) A pharmacist with your full medication list
B) Social media health forums
C) Only the drug manufacturer hotline
D) No one — interactions are rare

answer: A
explanation: Pharmacists are trained to identify interactions when they know all medicines and supplements you use. Forums lack your personal history; manufacturers cannot review your full regimen, and interactions are common enough to warrant screening.

## Question 3

How can NSAIDs like ibuprofen interact with some blood pressure medicines?

A) They always lower blood pressure further
B) They may reduce kidney blood flow and affect blood pressure control
C) They have no effect on kidneys
D) They replace the need for blood pressure drugs

answer: B
explanation: NSAIDs can reduce prostaglandin-mediated kidney blood flow, which may worsen blood pressure control or kidney function in susceptible people. They do not reliably lower BP, are not kidney-neutral, and never replace prescribed therapy.

## Question 4

Why tell providers about herbal supplements when taking prescriptions?

A) Supplements never interact with drugs
B) Some supplements like St. John's wort can alter prescription drug levels
C) Only vitamins matter, not herbs
D) Providers already know every supplement you take

answer: B
explanation: Herbal products can induce or inhibit drug metabolism — St. John's wort is a well-known example. Supplements can interact; herbs are not exempt; providers do not automatically know what you take unless you tell them.

## Question 5

What should you do before adding a new OTC medicine if you take several prescriptions?

A) Assume OTC is always safe
B) Ask a pharmacist or clinician to review for interactions
C) Double all prescription doses instead
D) Stop all prescriptions for one day

answer: B
explanation: Professional review catches interaction risks with your specific regimen. OTC is not automatically safe with prescriptions; changing doses or stopping prescribed drugs without guidance is dangerous.

## pain-medications-safely

| passScore | 70                             |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What organ is most at risk from too much acetaminophen?

A) Heart
B) Liver
C) Kidneys
D) Lungs

answer: B
explanation: Acetaminophen is processed by the liver. Taking more than the daily limit — especially from multiple products — can cause serious liver damage. The heart, kidneys, and lungs are not the primary organs at risk from acetaminophen overdose.

## Question 2

Why check cold medicine labels for acetaminophen?

A) It is always safe to combine
B) Multiple products can exceed daily limits
C) It only matters for children
D) Labels are optional

answer: B
explanation: Many cold, flu, and pain products contain acetaminophen under different brand names. Adding them together can push you past the safe daily limit without realizing it. Always read active ingredients on every label.

## Question 3

When should you avoid ibuprofen without medical advice?

A) Mild headache
B) Known kidney disease or stomach ulcers
C) After exercise
D) When food is available

answer: B
explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen can worsen kidney function and irritate the stomach lining. People with kidney disease, stomach ulcers, or on blood thinners should only use them with medical guidance. A mild headache in someone without those conditions is different.

## Question 4

What should you do for chest pain?

A) Take extra pain medicine and wait
B) Seek emergency care immediately
C) Only use ice packs
D) Ignore it if you are young

answer: B
explanation: Chest pain can signal a heart attack or other life-threatening condition. Pain medicine will not fix the underlying emergency. Call 911 or go to the emergency room immediately — do not wait to see if it passes.

## Question 5

Why tell your pharmacist all medicines you take?

A) To check interactions and duplications
B) Pharmacies sell more products
C) It is not necessary for OTC drugs
D) Only for prescriptions from one doctor

answer: A
explanation: Pharmacists check for duplicate ingredients (like acetaminophen in multiple products) and dangerous drug interactions. This is especially important when you take prescriptions, OTC medicines, and supplements together.

## reading-lab-report

| passScore | 70                   |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What does an H flag usually mean?

A) Healthy
B) High relative to reference range
C) Hospital only
D) Hormone test only

answer: B
explanation: An H or L flag means your result is outside the lab's reference range — high or low compared to typical values. It is a signal to discuss with your doctor, not an automatic diagnosis.

## Question 2

Reference ranges:

A) Are identical in every lab worldwide
B) Can vary by lab and patient factors
C) Replace medical advice
D) Mean you definitely have disease if outside

answer: B
explanation: Reference ranges vary by laboratory equipment, age, sex, and pregnancy status. A number slightly outside range may be normal for you. Your doctor interprets results in context, not from the flag alone.

## Question 3

Why compare past results?

A) Never useful
B) Trends help show if values are changing over time
C) Only for children
D) Portals do this illegally

answer: B
explanation: A single abnormal value matters less than the trend over time. Rising glucose or falling hemoglobin across multiple tests tells a clearer story than one isolated result.

## Question 4

Slightly abnormal result — best first step?

A) Panic
B) Discuss with your doctor in context
C) Change dose yourself
D) Ignore forever

answer: B
explanation: Bring questions to your visit: what does this mean for me, do we repeat the test, could my medicines affect it? Self-treating based on a lab printout without medical context can be unsafe.

## Question 5

Critical value on portal with no call — you should:

A) Wait a month
B) Contact your care team promptly
C) Post online only
D) Retest at home only

answer: B
explanation: Critical or panic values — very high potassium, severe anemia, dangerous glucose — often trigger a call from the lab or doctor. If you see critical language, contact your care team promptly.

## reading-medical-bills

> Source file: `content/quizzes/en/reading-medical-bills.mdx`

| passScore | 70                           |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What should you check first when you receive a medical bill?

A) Whether the bill is printed on official letterhead
B) Whether your personal information, the dates of service, and the services listed are correct
C) Whether the bill has a watermark
D) Whether the envelope is sealed properly

answer: B
explanation: Always verify your name, the dates you received care, and the procedures listed. Mistakes in billing are common. An incorrect date, wrong procedure code, or mixed-up patient information can lead to being charged for services you did not receive.

## Question 2

What is an Explanation of Benefits or EOB?

A) A bill that shows how much you owe
B) A summary from your insurance company showing what services were billed, what was covered, and what you may owe
C) A letter explaining why your insurance was denied
D) A form you fill out to apply for insurance

answer: B
explanation: An EOB is not a bill. It is a statement from your insurance explaining how a claim was processed. It shows the amount billed, the insurance discount, what the insurance paid, and your remaining responsibility. Compare it with the providers bill to check for errors.

## Question 3

What does a "CPT code" on a medical bill represent?

A) The patients condition or diagnosis
B) A standard code that describes the medical procedure or service that was provided
C) The doctors license number
D) The hospitals room number

answer: B
explanation: CPT codes are standardized numbers assigned to every medical procedure and service, like a 99213 for an office visit. These codes determine how much you are charged and whether your insurance will cover the service. Errors in coding can lead to incorrect charges.

## Question 4

If you cannot afford to pay a medical bill, what should you do?

A) Ignore it and hope it goes away
B) Contact the billing office to ask about payment plans or financial assistance
C) Pay only half and assume that is enough
D) Dispute the entire bill without any reason

answer: B
explanation: Most hospitals and medical providers offer payment plans or charity care programs for patients who cannot pay their full bill. Contact the billing office and ask about options. Ignoring the bill can lead to collection actions and damage to your credit.

## Question 5

What is a common reason medical bills contain errors?

A) Hospitals intentionally overcharge all patients
B) Billing is complex and errors like duplicate charges, wrong codes, or incorrect insurance information are common
C) Doctors do not know how much services cost
D) Insurance companies refuse to share information

answer: B
explanation: Medical billing is complicated and error-prone. Common mistakes include duplicate charges for the same service, upcoding (billing for a more expensive service than was provided), and incorrect insurance information. Reviewing bills carefully can save you money.

## reading-nutrition-labels

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is the first thing you should look at on a nutrition facts label?

A) The brand name
B) The serving size and the number of servings per container
C) The expiration date
D) The ingredient list in small font

answer: B
explanation: Serving size is the foundation of the nutrition label. All the information on the label is based on one serving. If you eat two servings, you need to double all the numbers. Many packages that look like single servings actually contain multiple servings.

## Question 2

What does the "% Daily Value" tell you on a nutrition label?

A) The exact number of calories you should eat each day
B) How much a nutrient in one serving contributes to a daily diet based on a 2,000-calorie diet
C) The percentage of the food that is fat
D) The amount of sugar you should eat per day

answer: B
explanation: Percent Daily Value shows how much a nutrient in one serving contributes to a total daily diet. A DV of 5 percent or less is low, and 20 percent or more is high. Use this to quickly compare foods and see if they are high or low in specific nutrients.

## Question 3

Which of the following nutrients should you try to limit according to the nutrition label?

A) Dietary fiber
B) Vitamin D
C) Saturated fat, sodium, and added sugars
D) Potassium

answer: C
explanation: Health experts recommend limiting saturated fat, sodium, and added sugars because they are linked to heart disease, high blood pressure, and other health problems. Look for low DV percentages for these nutrients. Fiber, vitamins, and minerals are beneficial.

## Question 4

What is the difference between "total sugars" and "added sugars" on a label?

A) They are the same thing
B) Total sugars includes natural and added sugars; added sugars shows how much sugar was added during processing
C) Added sugars only includes artificial sweeteners
D) Total sugars does not include sugar from fruit

answer: B
explanation: Total sugars includes both naturally occurring sugars found in foods like fruit and dairy plus any sugars added during processing. Added sugars specifically shows how much sugar was added. The American Heart Association recommends limiting added sugars.

## Question 5

Why is the ingredient list important on a food package?

A) It shows the brand name
B) Ingredients are listed in descending order by weight, so the first ingredients make up the most of the food
C) It tells you when the food was manufactured
D) It lists the price per ingredient

answer: B
explanation: Ingredients are listed from the most to the least by weight. If sugar or a type of oil is listed first, the product is mostly made of that ingredient. This helps you identify hidden sources of sugar, unhealthy fats, and artificial additives.

## sleep-and-health

> Source file: `content/quizzes/en/sleep-and-health.mdx`
