### Quiz Content

## Question 1

How many hours of sleep do most adults need per night?

A) 4 to 5 hours
B) 7 to 9 hours
C) 10 to 12 hours
D) 5 to 6 hours

answer: B
explanation: Most adults need 7 to 9 hours of quality sleep per night for optimal health. Consistent sleep helps your body repair, supports brain function, and strengthens your immune system. Sleeping too little over time increases health risks.

## Question 2

What is sleep hygiene?

A) Washing your bedsheets every night
B) Habits and practices that promote good, consistent sleep
C) A special diet for people who cannot sleep
D) Using medication to fall asleep faster

answer: B
explanation: Sleep hygiene refers to healthy sleep habits like keeping a consistent bedtime, avoiding screens before bed, limiting caffeine in the evening, and creating a cool, dark, quiet sleep environment. Good sleep hygiene helps you fall asleep and stay asleep.

## Question 3

How does chronic lack of sleep affect your health?

A) It has no effect on health
B) It increases the risk of obesity, heart disease, diabetes, and weakened immune function
C) It only affects your mood, not your physical health
D) It improves memory and concentration

answer: B
explanation: Chronic sleep deprivation is linked to serious health problems including obesity, heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, and depression. It also weakens the immune system, making you more likely to get sick.

## Question 4

What is sleep apnea?

A) A condition where you cannot fall asleep at night
B) A disorder where breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep
C) A condition where you sleep too much
D) A temporary phase of insomnia

answer: B
explanation: Sleep apnea causes repeated pauses in breathing during sleep, which reduces oxygen levels and disrupts sleep quality. Common signs include loud snoring, gasping for air during sleep, and daytime fatigue. It can increase the risk of heart problems if untreated.

## Question 5

What should you avoid before bedtime to improve sleep?

A) Reading a book
B) Using phones, tablets, or computers because blue light can interfere with your body's sleep signals
C) Drinking herbal tea
D) Taking a warm bath

answer: B
explanation: Blue light from screens suppresses melatonin, the hormone that signals your body to sleep. Avoiding screens for at least 30 to 60 minutes before bed, along with limiting caffeine and heavy meals, helps you fall asleep more easily.

## sleep-apnea-basics

| passScore | 70                   |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Obstructive sleep apnea is caused by:

A) Dreaming too much
B) Blocked airflow when throat muscles relax
C) Too much caffeine only
D) Normal snoring always

answer: B
explanation: Obstructive sleep apnea happens when throat muscles relax during sleep and block airflow. The brain briefly wakes you to breathe again. It is not simply snoring — it involves repeated breathing pauses.

## Question 2

A reason to seek evaluation:

A) Snoring plus daytime sleepiness
B) One night of poor sleep
C) Occasional yawn
D) Reading before bed

answer: A
explanation: Loud snoring plus daytime sleepiness, morning headaches, or a partner noticing breathing pauses are common warning signs. Snoring alone does not always mean apnea, but the combination warrants evaluation.

## Question 3

CPAP works by:

A) Surgery on the throat
B) Delivering air pressure to keep the airway open
C) Replacing all exercise
D) Stopping breathing on purpose

answer: B
explanation: CPAP delivers steady air pressure through a mask to keep the airway open during sleep. It is the most common effective treatment for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea — not a cure, but a nightly therapy.

## Question 4

Untreated sleep apnea increases risk of:

A) Only dry skin
B) High blood pressure and heart disease among others
C) Improved driving
D) Lower weight always

answer: B
explanation: Untreated sleep apnea is linked to high blood pressure, heart disease, stroke risk, and poor glucose control. Treating it protects more than sleep quality — it supports cardiovascular and metabolic health.

## Question 5

If CPAP is uncomfortable:

A) Stop forever without telling anyone
B) Ask a sleep specialist about mask fit and alternatives
C) Drive long trips while drowsy
D) Only use it once a month

answer: B
explanation: Mask fit, humidity settings, and alternative devices (oral appliances, positional therapy) can improve comfort. A sleep specialist can adjust settings — stopping CPAP without guidance usually brings symptoms back.

| lessonId  | "smoking-cessation-medicines"      |
| passScore | 70                                 |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which are FDA-approved smoking cessation medicines?

A) Nicotine replacement, varenicline, and bupropion
B) Only unregulated herbal cigarettes
C) High-dose antibiotics
D) Daily aspirin as the sole quit therapy

answer: A
explanation: NRT, varenicline, and bupropion are established FDA-approved pharmacotherapies. Herbal cigarettes are not approved quit aids; antibiotics and aspirin alone are not standard cessation drugs.

## Question 2

How does nicotine replacement therapy help quitting?

A) Delivers controlled nicotine to reduce withdrawal while avoiding most cigarette toxins
B) Makes cigarettes taste better
C) Eliminates all nicotine addiction instantly in one day
D) Replaces the need for any behavioral support

answer: A
explanation: NRT eases withdrawal without most combustion toxins. It does not enhance cigarette flavor, does not instantly erase addiction, and works best combined with counseling per CDC.

## Question 3

What does the USPSTF recommend for adults who smoke?

A) Offer tobacco cessation interventions including pharmacotherapy when appropriate
B) Avoid discussing smoking until age 80
C) Only recommend quitting without any support tools
D) Discourage all quit attempts as futile

answer: A
explanation: USPSTF strongly recommends cessation support for all adult smokers. Clinicians should address smoking at relevant visits, not delay until old age, and evidence supports tools beyond willpower alone.

## Question 4

Why combine patch plus short-acting nicotine product?

A) Steady baseline plus relief for breakthrough cravings often improves quit rates
B) It guarantees instant harm from nicotine overdose always
C) Patches alone contain zero nicotine
D) Short-acting forms are only for non-smokers

answer: A
explanation: Combination NRT is a CDC-supported strategy for difficult cravings. Used correctly it is not designed to overdose; patches do deliver nicotine; short-acting NRT is for people quitting smoking.

## Question 5

What should you do if bupropion for quitting causes mood worsening?

A) Contact your clinician immediately — do not ignore psychiatric side effects
B) Double the dose to push through
C) Start smoking more to balance mood
D) Stop all medical care permanently

answer: A
explanation: Bupropion carries neuropsychiatric monitoring needs. Doubling dose worsens risk; smoking more undermines quitting; stopping all care is unsafe — clinician guidance is required.

| passScore | 70                              |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which test is commonly used first to screen thyroid function?

A) TSH
B) Cholesterol only
C) Blood type
D) Skin biopsy

answer: A
explanation: TSH is the primary screening test for hypo- and hyperthyroidism. Cholesterol may rise in hypothyroidism but is not the screen; blood type and skin biopsy do not assess thyroid function.

## Question 2

Which symptoms align more with hypothyroidism?

A) Fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance
B) Only fever and rash for 24 hours
C) Sudden face droop and arm weakness
D) Improved marathon speed without training

answer: A
explanation: Hypothyroidism slows metabolism causing fatigue, weight gain, and cold sensitivity. Brief fever/rash, stroke signs, and unexplained athletic gains are not typical hypothyroid patterns.

## Question 3

What is a standard treatment for hypothyroidism?

A) Levothyroxine hormone replacement
B) High-dose iodine for everyone
C) Avoiding all medical follow-up
D) Only aspirin daily

answer: A
explanation: Levothyroxine replaces deficient T4. Iodine helps only in deficiency states and can worsen some conditions; follow-up is required; aspirin does not treat hypothyroidism.

## Question 4

Why can hyperthyroidism be dangerous if untreated?

A) It can cause rapid heart rate and serious arrhythmias
B) It always lowers heart rate to zero safely
C) It only affects hair color
D) It prevents all infections permanently

answer: A
explanation: Excess thyroid hormone stresses the cardiovascular system. It increases rather than safely zeroes heart rate; effects extend beyond cosmetic hair changes; it does not confer infection immunity.

## Question 5

Why tell the lab if you take biotin supplements before thyroid blood work?

A) Biotin can falsely affect some immunoassay thyroid results
B) Biotin is required for accurate TSH always
C) Labs refuse all patients on vitamins
D) Biotin cures Graves' disease

answer: A
explanation: High-dose biotin interferes with certain thyroid immunoassays. It is not required for accuracy; labs do not refuse vitamin users; biotin is not a Graves' cure.

## type-1-vs-type-2-diabetes

> Source file: `content/quizzes/en/type-1-vs-type-2-diabetes.mdx`

| lessonId  | "type-1-vs-type-2-diabetes"      |
| passScore | 70                               |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What causes type 1 diabetes?

A) Autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic cells
B) Eating too much candy alone in every person
C) Only obesity in adults over 65
D) Lack of exercise for one week

answer: A
explanation: Type 1 is immune-mediated beta cell loss requiring insulin. Candy alone does not cause type 1; obesity is central to type 2 risk, not type 1 mechanism; brief inactivity does not explain type 1.

## Question 2

Which treatment is essential from diagnosis for type 1 diabetes?

A) Insulin therapy
B) Only herbal supplements
C) Avoiding all carbohydrates forever
D) No monitoring needed

answer: A
explanation: Type 1 always needs insulin for survival. Supplements cannot replace insulin; zero-carb diets are not standard mandatory therapy; monitoring is essential for safety.

## Question 3

What best describes type 2 diabetes pathophysiology?

A) Insulin resistance with progressive insulin secretory decline
B) Complete absence of any insulin from birth in all cases
C) Only a viral infection lasting two days
D) Exclusively a childhood autoimmune disease

answer: A
explanation: Type 2 combines resistance and relative insulin deficiency over time. Total absence from birth describes type 1; brief viruses and childhood autoimmunity do not define type 2.

## Question 4

Why is distinguishing type 1 from type 2 clinically important?

A) Treatment and urgency differ — insulin is lifesaving in type 1
B) Both are identical and need no insulin ever
C) Only type 2 requires any medical follow-up
D) Type 1 never causes emergencies

answer: A
explanation: Misclassification risks DKA if type 1 is untreated with insulin. Types differ; both need follow-up; type 1 can cause rapid emergencies without insulin.

## Question 5

Which statement about sugar and diabetes is most accurate?

A) Sugar alone directly causes all diabetes types
B) Type 2 risk is multifactorial; type 1 is not caused by sugar intake alone
C) Only people who never eat sugar get diabetes
D) Sugar has no effect on blood glucose in any person

answer: B
explanation: Sugar affects glucose levels but does not singularly cause type 1 or all type 2. Avoiding sugar entirely does not guarantee prevention; sugar clearly impacts blood glucose.

| passScore | 70                       |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What time period does A1c roughly reflect?

A) Average blood glucose over about 2 to 3 months
B) Only the last meal eaten
C) Blood pressure over one week
D) Cholesterol for six years

answer: A
explanation: A1c integrates glycation over red blood cell lifespan (~120 days). It is not meal-specific, does not measure BP, and is unrelated to cholesterol duration.

## Question 2

Which A1c range does ADA use for prediabetes?

A) 5.7% to 6.4%
B) Below 4.0%
C) 8.0% to 9.0% only
D) Exactly 10% always

answer: A
explanation: ADA prediabetes is 5.7–6.4%; diabetes ≥6.5%. Below 4% is abnormally low; 8–10% suggests diabetes, not prediabetes band definition.

## Question 3

At what A1c is diabetes generally diagnosed (with confirmation rules)?

A) 6.5% or higher
B) 4.0% exactly
C) 3.0% or lower
D) 9.9% only on Tuesdays

answer: A
explanation: ADA diagnostic threshold for diabetes is A1c ≥6.5% with repeat confirmation when asymptomatic. 4% and 3% are not diabetes thresholds; arbitrary day-specific cutoffs are not clinical criteria.

## Question 4

Why might A1c disagree with daily glucose meter readings?

A) Anemia or hemoglobin variants can falsely lower or raise A1c
B) Meters and A1c always match perfectly
C) A1c measures insulin dose directly
D) Home glucose never varies

answer: A
explanation: RBC turnover and hemoglobin variants affect glycation measurement. Perfect match is not guaranteed; A1c is not an insulin assay; home glucose varies daily.

## Question 5

Why act on prediabetes even without symptoms?

A) Lifestyle change can slow or prevent progression to type 2 diabetes
B) Prediabetes means you already need insulin always
C) A1c cannot detect prediabetes
D) Only children get prediabetes

answer: A
explanation: DPP and CDC programs show progression can be reduced. Prediabetes does not mandate immediate insulin; A1c defines prediabetes band; adults commonly have prediabetes.

## understanding-allergies

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is anaphylaxis?

A) A mild seasonal allergy
B) A severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction
C) A type of food intolerance
D) A skin rash that always goes away on its own

answer: B
explanation: Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction that can affect breathing and blood pressure and requires emergency treatment.

## Question 2

What should you do first if you have epinephrine and signs of anaphylaxis?

A) Wait to see if symptoms improve
B) Use epinephrine as directed and call 911
C) Take only an antihistamine
D) Drive yourself to urgent care

answer: B
explanation: Epinephrine is first-line emergency treatment for anaphylaxis. Call 911 because a second wave of symptoms can occur.

## Question 3

Why tell every doctor and pharmacist about your allergies?

A) It is only required for food allergies
B) To avoid medicines or products that could trigger a reaction
C) Pharmacies already have this information automatically
D) It is only needed for children

answer: B
explanation: Drug and latex allergies are common. Providers need your full allergy history to prescribe and dispense safely.

## Question 4

Which is an example of an environmental allergy trigger?

A) Penicillin
B) Pollen
C) Shellfish
D) Latex gloves only

answer: B
explanation: Pollen is a common environmental allergen. Medicines, foods, and latex are other categories of triggers.

## Question 5

Why is self-diagnosing food allergies risky?

A) All food allergies are mild
B) Eliminating foods without testing can cause nutritional gaps and miss other conditions
C) Doctors cannot test for food allergies
D) Food labels list all allergens in every country

answer: B
explanation: Professional evaluation helps confirm true allergies and safe diets. Unnecessary restriction can harm nutrition.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What does a CBC primarily measure?

A) Blood cells including RBCs, WBCs, and platelets
B) Cholesterol and triglycerides only
C) Kidney function creatinine only
D) Thyroid hormone TSH only

answer: A
explanation: CBC counts cellular blood components. Lipid panels, creatinine, and TSH are separate tests — not components of a standard CBC.

## Question 2

Low hemoglobin on a CBC most often suggests which condition?

A) Anemia
B) High blood sugar diabetes
C) Broken bone
D) Seasonal allergy

answer: A
explanation: Hemoglobin carries oxygen; low values define anemia. Diabetes, fractures, and allergies are not directly diagnosed by low hemoglobin alone on CBC.

## Question 3

Why might white blood cell count be elevated?

A) Infection, inflammation, or physiological stress
B) Only because of drinking water
C) Always means leukemia with no other causes
D) WBC never changes in illness

answer: A
explanation: Leukocytosis commonly follows infection and inflammation. Hydration alone does not typically spike WBC; leukemia is one rare cause among many; WBC clearly shifts with illness.

## Question 4

Why should you avoid starting iron supplements solely because of fatigue?

A) Anemia cause should be confirmed — excess iron can be harmful
B) Iron never treats anemia
C) CBC never detects low hemoglobin
D) Fatigue only comes from lack of sleep always

answer: A
explanation: Iron helps iron-deficiency anemia but harms if given unnecessarily. Iron does treat deficiency; CBC detects low hemoglobin; fatigue has many causes beyond sleep alone.

## Question 5

What do low platelets (thrombocytopenia) increase risk for?

A) Bleeding and bruising
B) Improved blood clotting always
C) Higher oxygen saturation automatically
D) Lower infection risk always

answer: A
explanation: Platelets enable clotting; low counts raise bleeding risk. Thrombocytopenia does not improve clotting, raise SpO2, or universally prevent infection.

| passScore | 70                               |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is a common goal of manufacturer copay cards?

A) Replace insurance entirely
B) Lower patient out-of-pocket cost for a specific drug
C) Increase drug prices
D) Eliminate need for prescriptions

answer: B
explanation: Manufacturer copay cards reduce what you pay at the pharmacy for a specific brand drug. They do not replace insurance or eliminate the need for a valid prescription — they lower your out-of-pocket share for eligible patients.

## Question 2

What should you do before stopping a medicine you cannot afford?

A) Stop immediately
B) Talk with your doctor about alternatives and assistance
C) Buy from unknown online sellers only
D) Double the dose to make it last

answer: B
explanation: Stopping a needed medicine suddenly can be dangerous. Your doctor may know about generics, alternative doses, samples, or assistance programs. Always discuss affordability before changing or stopping treatment.

## Question 3

Why be cautious with unsolicited copay help calls?

A) They are always legitimate
B) Scams may ask for sensitive personal information
C) Pharmacies never offer real programs
D) Insurance forbids all assistance

answer: B
explanation: Legitimate programs use official websites and clinic financial counselors. Scammers may ask for your Social Security number, bank details, or payment upfront. Never share sensitive information with unsolicited callers.

## Question 4

Who can help navigate assistance at many hospitals?

A) Only the billing department after discharge
B) Financial counselor or social worker
C) No one — you must figure it out alone
D) Only drug sales representatives

answer: B
explanation: Hospital financial counselors and social workers know manufacturer programs, nonprofit grants, and local resources. They can help you apply without navigating complex rules alone — ask at registration or billing.

## Question 5

Why re-check assistance eligibility yearly?

A) Programs never change
B) Insurance, income rules, and program funding can change
C) Once approved, it lasts forever
D) Doctors handle this automatically

answer: B
explanation: Assistance programs depend on insurance type, income limits, and manufacturer funding. A change in your job, Medicare status, or plan design can end eligibility. Re-check each year and when your coverage changes.

## understanding-depression

| id        | "understanding-depression"      |
| title     | "Understanding Depression Quiz" |
| lessonId  | "understanding-depression"      |
| passScore | 70                              |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is depression?

A) The same as feeling sad for a few hours after a bad day
B) A common but serious mood disorder that affects how you feel, think, and handle daily activities
C) A sign of personal weakness
D) An illness that only affects older adults

answer: B
explanation: Depression is a medical condition, not a character flaw or temporary sadness. It involves persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest in activities, and changes in sleep, appetite, and energy. It affects people of all ages and backgrounds.

## Question 2

Which of the following is a common symptom of depression?

A) Feeling unusually happy and energetic for weeks
B) Persistent sadness, loss of interest in hobbies, and changes in sleep or appetite
C) Sudden improvement in memory and concentration
D) Increased desire to socialize with others

answer: B
explanation: Common depression symptoms include persistent sadness or emptiness, loss of interest in activities once enjoyed, significant changes in weight or appetite, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, low energy, difficulty concentrating, and thoughts of death or suicide.

## Question 3

How is depression typically treated?

A) Depression does not need treatment; it goes away on its own
B) Through therapy, medication, or a combination of both
C) Only by taking herbal supplements
D) By exercising for 12 hours a day

answer: B
explanation: Depression is highly treatable. The most effective approaches include psychotherapy or talk therapy, antidepressant medication, or both. Lifestyle changes like regular exercise and social support also help. What works best varies from person to person.

## Question 4

If someone says they are thinking about suicide, what should you do?

A) Ignore it because people who talk about suicide rarely mean it
B) Take it seriously, stay with them, and help them contact a crisis helpline or emergency services
C) Tell them to think about something else
D) Wait to see if they mention it again

answer: B
explanation: Any mention of suicide should be taken seriously. Stay with the person and call or text 988 (the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline) or 911. Do not leave them alone. Talking about suicide does not increase the risk; it provides an opportunity to help.

## Question 5

Can depression affect physical health?

A) No, depression is only in your mind
B) Yes, depression can cause physical symptoms like headaches, digestive problems, and chronic pain
C) No, mental health and physical health are completely separate
D) Yes, but only in people over 60

answer: B
explanation: Depression affects both mind and body. It can cause fatigue, headaches, back pain, digestive issues, and worsen chronic conditions like heart disease or diabetes. Treating depression often improves both mental and physical health.

## understanding-health-insurance

| title     | "Understanding Health Insurance Quiz" |
| lessonId  | "understanding-health-insurance"      |
| passScore | 70                                    |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is a health insurance premium?

A) The amount you pay when you visit the doctor
B) The monthly payment you make to keep your insurance active
C) The discount you get for using in-network providers
D) The total amount your employer pays for your healthcare

answer: B
explanation: A premium is the amount you pay each month to have health insurance coverage. You pay this whether or not you use medical services. Premiums vary based on the plan type, coverage level, and your age or location.

## Question 2

What is a deductible in health insurance?

A) The amount you pay each time you fill a prescription
B) The amount you must pay out of pocket before your insurance starts covering services
C) The monthly payment to keep your insurance
D) The maximum amount your insurance will pay in a year

answer: B
explanation: A deductible is the amount you pay for covered healthcare services before your insurance plan starts to pay. For example, if your deductible is 1,000 dollars, you pay the first 1,000 dollars of covered services yourself. Some preventive services are covered before you meet the deductible.

## Question 3

What does "in-network" mean?

A) Doctors and hospitals that have a contract with your insurance plan to provide care at lower rates
B) Any doctor or hospital you choose to visit
C) A special network of doctors who only treat emergencies
D) Online doctors who you can only see through a computer

answer: A
explanation: In-network providers have agreed to accept your insurance plans negotiated rates. Using in-network providers usually costs you much less than going out-of-network. Always check if your doctor is in-network before scheduling to avoid surprise bills.

## Question 4

What is a copay?

A) A fixed amount you pay for a specific service, like 20 dollars for a doctors visit
B) The total cost of your medical treatment
C) A discount you receive for paying your premium early
D) The amount your insurance pays to the hospital

answer: A
explanation: A copay is a fixed dollar amount you pay at the time of service, such as 20 dollars for a primary care visit or 10 dollars for a prescription. Copays are separate from deductibles and usually do not count toward the deductible.

## Question 5

What is an out-of-pocket maximum?

A) The amount you can save by using insurance
B) The most you will have to pay for covered services in a plan year
C) The amount you owe if you cancel your insurance
D) The maximum amount your insurance pays for a single procedure

answer: B
explanation: The out-of-pocket maximum is the most you will pay for covered healthcare services in a year. Once you reach this limit, your insurance pays 100 percent of covered services for the rest of the plan year. This protects you from catastrophic medical costs.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which lipoprotein is most associated with artery plaque buildup when elevated?

A) LDL cholesterol
B) HDL cholesterol
C) Vitamin D
D) Sodium

answer: A
explanation: High LDL promotes atherosclerotic plaque. HDL generally helps remove cholesterol from arteries; vitamin D and sodium are not lipoprotein cholesterol types.

## Question 2

What do very high triglycerides (e.g., above 500 mg/dL) especially risk?

A) Pancreatitis
B) Improved athletic performance only
C) Lower stroke risk automatically
D) No health effects

answer: A
explanation: Severely elevated triglycerides increase acute pancreatitis risk. They do not improve performance by themselves, do not automatically lower stroke risk, and clearly have health effects.

## Question 3

How do ACC/AHA guidelines typically use LDL results?

A) As the only factor in every decision
B) Within overall cardiovascular risk assessment
C) They ignore LDL completely
D) Only for patients under age 18

answer: B
explanation: Guidelines integrate LDL with age, BP, diabetes, smoking, and other factors. LDL alone is not the sole driver; LDL is central, not ignored; lipid management applies across adult ages per risk.

## Question 4

Which lifestyle change can improve lipid profiles?

A) Regular physical activity and heart-healthy eating
B) Eliminating all dietary fat regardless of type
C) Avoiding all medical screening
D) Increasing added sugars for energy

answer: A
explanation: Activity and Mediterranean-style patterns lower LDL and triglycerides in many people. Not all fats are harmful; screening guides care; added sugars can worsen triglycerides.

## Question 5

What does HDL cholesterol generally do?

A) Helps transport cholesterol away from arteries
B) Directly clogs arteries when any amount is present
C) Is identical to LDL in function
D) Measures blood sugar control

answer: A
explanation: HDL participates in reverse cholesterol transport. It does not clog arteries by mere presence, is functionally different from LDL, and does not reflect glucose control (that is A1c).

## understanding-oxygen-saturation

| id        | "understanding-oxygen-saturation"      |
| title     | "Understanding Oxygen Saturation Quiz" |

| passScore | 70                                     |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What does a pulse oximeter SpO2 reading represent?

A) Estimated percentage of hemoglobin carrying oxygen
B) Blood sugar level
C) Heart valve function directly
D) Liver enzyme activity

answer: A
explanation: SpO2 reflects oxyhemoglobin saturation via light absorption. It does not measure glucose, valve anatomy directly, or hepatic enzymes.

## Question 2

Which SpO2 range is typical for healthy adults at sea level?

A) About 95% to 100%
B) 50% to 60%
C) Exactly 70% always
D) Below 40% normally

answer: A
explanation: NIH cites roughly 95–100% as normal adult sea-level SpO2. 50–60%, fixed 70%, or below 40% indicate serious hypoxemia, not normal wellness.

## Question 3

When is SpO2 below 90% especially concerning?

A) When accompanied by shortness of breath or other acute symptoms
B) Only when measured during sleep in all people always
C) Never — any reading is fine
D) Only in people wearing glasses

answer: A
explanation: Hypoxemia with dyspnea or chest symptoms warrants urgent evaluation. Low SpO2 is not always benign during sleep for everyone; very low values are never fine; glasses do not define hypoxemia risk.

## Question 4

What can falsely lower pulse oximeter accuracy?

A) Cold fingers, poor circulation, or dark nail polish
B) Drinking water before the reading
C) Sitting quietly with warm hands
D) Using a calibrated device on the index finger

answer: A
explanation: Poor perfusion and nail pigment interfere with light signals. Hydration and proper warm still measurement improve accuracy; calibrated proper use is best practice, not a source of error.

## Question 5

Why can a normal SpO2 still require medical attention?

A) Severe breathing trouble can occur before numbers drop in some conditions
B) Oximeters diagnose every disease perfectly
C) SpO2 above 100% is common and harmless always
D) Carbon monoxide effects never matter

answer: A
explanation: Clinical distress matters beyond one number; oximeters are imperfect; SpO2 cannot exceed 100% meaningfully; carbon monoxide can cause tissue hypoxia with misleadingly normal SpO2.

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What does "Rx" on a prescription label mean?

A) Remedy X-ray
B) Prescription (from Latin _recipere_)
C) Required eXtract
D) Repeat dosage

answer: B
explanation: "Rx" comes from the Latin word _recipere_, meaning "to take." It is the standard abbreviation for a medical prescription.

## Question 2

Which part of the prescription label tells you how often to take your medication?

A) Patient name
B) Pharmacy name
C) Dosage instructions
D) Refill count

answer: C
explanation: The dosage instructions (or sig) tell you how much to take, how often, and by which route. Patient and pharmacy details are identifiers, and refill count shows remaining authorizations.

## Question 3

What does "NDC" stand for on a prescription label?

A) National Drug Code
B) New Dosage Calculation
C) Named Drug Classification
D) Non-Drowsy Compound

answer: A
explanation: The NDC is a unique identifier for the medication, including the manufacturer, product, and package size. It helps prevent dispensing errors.

## Question 4

If your label says "Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily," when should you take it?

A) Every 2 hours
B) Once in the morning and once at night
C) Only when symptoms appear
D) Every 12 hours exactly

answer: B
explanation: "Twice daily" usually means morning and evening, approximately 10-12 hours apart. Taking with meals can help you remember.

## Question 5

What should you do if the medication name on the label does not match what your doctor said?

A) Take it anyway
B) Call your pharmacist before taking it
C) Look it up online
D) Wait until your next appointment

answer: B
explanation: Always verify with your pharmacist if the medication name looks different from what you expected. The generic name may differ from the brand name, but it is safest to confirm.

## Question 6

Why is the expiration date important on a prescription label?

A) It is optional
B) The medication may be less effective or unsafe after this date
C) It tells you when to refill
D) It shows when the pharmacy opened the bottle

answer: B
explanation: Expired medications can lose potency or degrade into harmful compounds. Always check the expiration date and properly dispose of expired medicines.

## Question 7

What do the warning labels on a prescription bottle indicate?

A) The cost of the medication
B) Special precautions like drowsiness or avoiding alcohol
C) The manufacturer's address
D) How to refill

answer: B
explanation: Warning labels highlight specific safety precautions such as "may cause drowsiness," "avoid alcohol," or "take with food." Always read these before starting a new medication.

## Question 8

What information is NOT typically found on a prescription label?

A) Prescribing doctor's name
B) Pharmacy phone number
C) Medication cost
D) Refill information

answer: C
explanation: Prescription labels include the patient name, doctor name, pharmacy details, medication name, dosage, instructions, and refill info — but not the cost. The pharmacy can provide pricing separately.

## Question 9

If your label says "May cause drowsiness," what should you avoid?

A) Drinking water
B) Driving or operating heavy machinery
C) Eating food
D) Taking other medications

answer: B
explanation: Drowsiness warnings mean the medication can impair your alertness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how the medicine affects you.

## Question 10

What does the refill number on a label tell you?

A) How many times you can refill the prescription
B) When the medication expires
C) The pharmacy's refill policy
D) The doctor's DEA number

answer: A
explanation: The refill count shows how many additional times you can get the same prescription refilled without seeing your doctor. "Refills: 0" means you need a new prescription.

## understanding-type2-diabetes

| passScore | 70                                   |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What happens in the body of someone with type 2 diabetes?

A) The body produces too much insulin
B) The body becomes resistant to insulin or does not produce enough insulin to control blood sugar
C) The body cannot digest carbohydrates at all
D) The body stops producing red blood cells

answer: B
explanation: In type 2 diabetes, your cells become resistant to insulin, a hormone that helps sugar enter your cells for energy. Over time, the pancreas cannot produce enough insulin to keep blood sugar levels normal. This leads to high blood sugar.

## Question 2

What is a common symptom of uncontrolled high blood sugar?

A) Weight gain and slow heart rate
B) Frequent urination, excessive thirst, and unexplained weight loss
C) Improved vision and hearing
D) Decreased appetite and difficulty sleeping

answer: B
explanation: When blood sugar is high, your kidneys work overtime to remove excess sugar through urine. This causes frequent urination and thirst. Other symptoms include fatigue, blurry vision, and slow-healing cuts. These symptoms develop gradually in type 2 diabetes.

## Question 3

How can diet help manage type 2 diabetes?

A) Eating only one meal per day
B) Avoiding all carbohydrates completely
C) Eating balanced meals with controlled portions, limiting sugar and refined carbs
D) Drinking only fruit juice

answer: C
explanation: A diabetes-friendly diet focuses on portion control, fiber-rich foods, lean protein, and healthy fats. Monitoring carbohydrate intake helps keep blood sugar stable. A registered dietitian can help create a personalized meal plan.

## Question 4

What is the A1C test?

A) A daily blood sugar test done with a finger stick
B) A blood test that measures average blood sugar levels over the past 2 to 3 months
C) A test for kidney function
D) A urine test for ketones

answer: B
explanation: The A1C test provides an average of your blood sugar levels over the past 2 to 3 months. It shows how well your diabetes is being managed. Most people with diabetes should have an A1C test at least twice a year.

## Question 5

What foot care practice is important for people with diabetes?

A) Walking barefoot to strengthen the feet
B) Checking feet daily for cuts, blisters, or sores
C) Soaking feet in hot water every night
D) Applying ice to the feet before bed

answer: B
explanation: Diabetes can reduce blood flow and sensation in the feet, making it hard to feel injuries. Small cuts can become infected and lead to serious complications. Daily foot checks help catch problems early before they become severe.

## understanding-vaccines

> Source file: `content/quizzes/en/understanding-vaccines.mdx`

| passScore | 70                            |

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

How do vaccines work to protect you from disease?

A) They cure diseases after you get sick
B) They train your immune system to recognize and fight specific germs
C) They create a barrier on your skin that blocks germs
D) They replace your bodys natural immune system

answer: B
explanation: Vaccines contain weakened or inactivated parts of a germ. Your immune system learns to recognize the germ and builds antibodies against it. If you are later exposed to the real germ, your body can fight it off quickly.

## Question 2

What is herd immunity?

A) A type of vaccine given to farm animals
B) When most of a population is vaccinated, making it harder for disease to spread
C) Immunity that is passed down from parents to children
D) Natural immunity from getting sick

answer: B
explanation: Herd immunity occurs when a high percentage of a community is vaccinated, creating a barrier that slows or stops disease spread. This protects people who cannot get vaccinated, such as those with weakened immune systems or allergies.

## Question 3

Why are booster shots sometimes needed?

A) Vaccines expire like food does
B) Immunity from some vaccines can fade over time, and boosters strengthen the protection
C) Boosters are optional and do not provide additional protection
D) Boosters are only for children, never for adults

answer: B
explanation: For some vaccines, immunity decreases over time. A booster shot reminds your immune system to produce more antibodies, keeping you protected. Examples include tetanus boosters every 10 years and COVID-19 boosters.

## Question 4

Which of the following is true about vaccine side effects?

A) Vaccines cause the disease they are meant to prevent in most people
B) Most side effects are mild and short-lived, like soreness at the injection site or low fever
C) Vaccines have no side effects at all
D) Side effects are always severe and dangerous

answer: B
explanation: Common vaccine side effects include soreness, redness at the injection site, and mild fever. These are normal signs that your immune system is responding. Serious side effects are extremely rare compared to the risks of the diseases vaccines prevent.

## Question 5

Which vaccine is recommended annually for most people?

A) The tetanus vaccine
B) The flu (influenza) vaccine
C) The hepatitis B vaccine
D) The polio vaccine

answer: B
explanation: The flu vaccine is recommended every year because flu viruses change over time. Each years vaccine is updated to match the strains expected to be most common. Annual vaccination gives you the best protection against the current flu season.

## when-to-call-911

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which of the following is a reason to call 911?

A) You have a mild cold and want to see a doctor
B) Someone is unconscious, not breathing, or having chest pain
C) You need a ride to the pharmacy
D) Your internet service is not working

answer: B
explanation: Call 911 for any life-threatening emergency: difficulty breathing, chest pain, signs of stroke, severe bleeding, choking, unconsciousness, or someone who stops breathing. When in doubt, call. Dispatchers can guide you on what to do while help arrives.

## Question 2

What should you do first when calling 911?

A) Hang up and call your doctor instead
B) Stay as calm as possible and clearly tell the dispatcher your location and what is happening
C) Start performing first aid before calling
D) Look up the nearest hospital address

answer: B
explanation: Stay calm and give the dispatcher your exact location and a clear description of the emergency. Answer their questions. They are trained to help you and will give instructions. Do not hang up until the dispatcher tells you to.

## Question 3

If someone is choking but is coughing forcefully, what should you do?

A) Perform the Heimlich maneuver immediately
B) Encourage them to keep coughing and stay with them
C) Call 911 right away
D） Give them water to drink

answer: B
explanation: If a choking person is coughing forcefully, their airway is partially blocked and they may be able to clear it on their own. Stay with them and encourage them to keep coughing. Only perform abdominal thrusts if they cannot cough, speak, or breathe.

## Question 4

When should you NOT call 911?

A) When someone is having a severe allergic reaction
B) When you have a minor cut that you can treat with a bandage at home
C) When you witness a car accident with injuries
D) When someone is having a stroke

answer: B
explanation: 911 is for emergencies that threaten life, limb, or property. Minor injuries that can be treated at home, routine medical questions, or non-urgent transportation needs should be handled through your primary care doctor or urgent care.

## Question 5

What information should you have ready when calling 911?

A) The patients favorite color
B) Your exact location, what happened, how many people are hurt, and the patients condition
C) The patients social security number
D) The patients blood type

answer: B
explanation: The dispatcher needs to know where to send help, what kind of emergency it is, and how many people are involved. Knowing the patients condition (conscious, breathing, bleeding) helps dispatchers send the right resources and give you instructions.

## when-to-use-urgent-care

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Urgent care is best for:

A) Chest pain and stroke
B) Same-day non-life-threatening problems
C) Annual physical exams
D) Routine prescription refills only

answer: B
explanation: Urgent care centers handle same-day problems that are not life-threatening — sprains, minor cuts, fever without severe distress, urinary symptoms. They bridge the gap when your doctor's office is closed.

## Question 2

Which belongs in the ER?

A) Mild sore throat
B) Severe trouble breathing
C) Small blister
D) Routine vaccination

answer: B
explanation: Severe trouble breathing, chest pain, stroke signs, heavy bleeding, and loss of consciousness need emergency care (911 or ER), not urgent care. Urgent care is not equipped for every emergency.

## Question 3

What does FAST stand for in stroke warning?

A) Face, Arm, Speech, Time to call 911
B) Food, Activity, Sleep, Temperature
C) Fever, Asthma, Stress, Tiredness
D) None of the above

answer: A
explanation: FAST reminds you: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 911. Stroke treatment is time-sensitive — minutes matter. Do not drive yourself if symptoms are sudden and severe.

## Question 4

Why follow up with primary care after urgent care?

A) Not necessary
B) To coordinate ongoing treatment and records
C) Urgent care replaces your doctor forever
D) Only for children

answer: B
explanation: Your primary care doctor coordinates long-term treatment and records. After urgent care, follow up so medications, referrals, and test results stay connected to your overall care plan.

## Question 5

When unsure about severity:

A) Wait days at home
B) Consider emergency care or call 911
C) Only use online forums
D) Skip all care

answer: B
explanation: High fever with stiff neck, confusion, or rash; injury with bone visible; or symptoms rapidly worsening may need ER-level care. When unsure, call 911 — dispatchers can help you decide.

## when-to-worry

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

Which of the following symptoms requires immediate emergency care?

A) A mild headache after a long day
B) Trouble breathing or shortness of breath that does not go away
C) A small paper cut on your finger
D) A stuffy nose from seasonal allergies

answer: B
explanation: Trouble breathing is a medical emergency that requires immediate attention. Call 911 or go to the emergency room if you have difficulty breathing, chest pain, or sudden confusion. Do not wait to see if it gets better on its own.

## Question 2

What should you do if you have a fever of 103 degrees Fahrenheit or higher?

A) Take a cold shower immediately
B) Wait one week to see if it goes down
C) Call your doctor or seek medical attention
D) Cover yourself with heavy blankets

answer: C
explanation: A fever of 103 degrees Fahrenheit or higher in adults requires medical attention. High fevers can indicate serious infections. Contact your doctor or seek medical care, especially if the fever is accompanied by other symptoms like stiff neck or confusion.

## Question 3

What is a sign that chest pain might be serious and require emergency care?

A) The pain goes away when you change position
B) The pain is sharp and lasts only a second
C) The pain is accompanied by shortness of breath, nausea, or pain spreading to the arm or jaw
D) The pain happens only when you take a deep breath

answer: C
explanation: Chest pain accompanied by shortness of breath, nausea, lightheadedness, or pain spreading to the arm, back, or jaw could be a heart attack. Call 911 immediately. Do not drive yourself to the hospital.

## Question 4

Which of the following sudden symptoms could indicate a stroke?

A) A mild muscle cramp in your leg
B) Numbness or weakness on one side of the face or body, confusion, or trouble speaking
C) A headache that goes away after drinking water
D) Blurred vision that clears up after blinking

answer: B
explanation: Use the FAST acronym to recognize stroke: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 911. Sudden numbness, confusion, trouble speaking, or vision changes require immediate emergency care.

## Question 5

If you cut yourself and the bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure, what should you do?

A) Keep applying pressure and seek medical help
B) Pour rubbing alcohol on the wound
C) Wait another hour to see if it stops
D) Remove the bandage and let the wound air dry

answer: A
explanation: If bleeding does not stop after 10 to 15 minutes of steady direct pressure, seek medical attention. You may need stitches or other treatment to close the wound and prevent excessive blood loss.

## why-preventive-care-matters

### Quiz Content

## Question 1

What is preventive care?

A) Treatment you receive after getting sick
B) Medical care focused on preventing illness or detecting it early before it becomes serious
C) Emergency care for life-threatening conditions
D) Alternative medicine that replaces regular doctor visits

answer: B
explanation: Preventive care includes check-ups, vaccinations, and screenings that help prevent disease or catch it early when it is easiest to treat. Regular preventive care can help you live a longer, healthier life.

## Question 2

Why are regular check-ups important even if you feel healthy?

A) They are not important if you feel fine
B) Some health problems have no symptoms in early stages and can only be detected through screenings
C) They are only required for people over age 65
D) They are mainly for getting free samples from the doctor

answer: B
explanation: Many serious conditions like high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and some cancers have no early symptoms. Regular check-ups and screenings can detect these problems early when treatment is most effective.

## Question 3

Under the Affordable Care Act, which preventive services are typically covered at no cost?

A) Only emergency room visits
B) Many preventive services like vaccines and cancer screenings are covered without a copay
C) No services are covered without cost
D) Only prescription medications

answer: B
explanation: The Affordable Care Act requires most insurance plans to cover recommended preventive services like annual check-ups, vaccines, and cancer screenings without charging a copay or deductible. This makes it easier for people to get preventive care.

## Question 4

How often should most adults have a routine physical exam?

A) Every 10 years
B) Only when they are sick
C) Once a year or as recommended by their doctor
D) Never, if they feel healthy

answer: C
explanation: Most adults should have an annual physical exam. Your doctor may recommend a different schedule based on your age, health conditions, and risk factors. Regular visits help track changes in your health over time.

## Question 5

What is a screening test?

A) A test that diagnoses a disease you already have symptoms for
B) A test that looks for disease in people who do not have symptoms yet
C) A test that determines your blood type
D) A test that measures your fitness level

answer: B
explanation: Screening tests are given to people without symptoms to detect potential health problems early. Examples include mammograms for breast cancer, colonoscopies for colon cancer, and blood pressure checks for hypertension.

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

Después de una visita al médico, ¿cuándo debe surtir una nueva receta?

A) Solo cuando se le acaben sus medicamentos actuales
B) Tan pronto como sea posible, idealmente el mismo día
C) Cuando se acuerde, incluso si es meses después
D) Solo si la farmacia ofrece un descuento

answer: B
explanation: Surtir su receta de inmediato asegura que no la olvide y comience su tratamiento a tiempo. También permite que el farmacéutico verifique interacciones farmacológicas y responda cualquier pregunta que pueda tener.

## Pregunta 2

¿Qué debe hacer si tiene preguntas sobre el resumen de su visita o las instrucciones de alta?

A) Ignorarlas y esperar lo mejor
B) Llamar al consultorio de su médico para aclarar antes de la próxima cita
C) Esperar hasta su próxima visita y preguntar entonces
D) Pedirle a un amigo que interprete los términos médicos

answer: B
explanation: Si algo en el resumen de su visita no está claro, llame al consultorio de su médico poco después de la visita. Obtener una aclaración rápidamente le ayuda a seguir su plan de cuidado correctamente y evitar errores con medicamentos o pasos de seguimiento.

## Pregunta 3

¿Por qué es importante programar su próxima cita de seguimiento antes de salir del consultorio?

A) Le ahorra una llamada telefónica después y asegura que obtenga una cita en un buen horario
B) El consultorio cobra menos si programa con anticipación
C) No es importante; puede llamar cuando quiera
D) El médico solo lo verá si programa antes de irse

answer: A
explanation: Programar su seguimiento antes de irse le garantiza un horario de cita conveniente y reduce la probabilidad de que olvide reservar una después. Mantener las citas de seguimiento es clave para manejar su salud.

## Pregunta 4

¿Qué debe hacer con los documentos médicos como órdenes de laboratorio o formularios de referencia después de su visita?

A) Tirarlos a la basura ya que todo es electrónico ahora
B) Guardarlos en una carpeta o archivo donde pueda encontrarlos fácilmente
C) Enviarlos por correo de vuelta al consultorio de su médico
D) Pegarlos en el refrigerador como recordatorio

answer: B
explanation: Guarde los documentos médicos importantes, las órdenes de laboratorio y los formularios de referencia en una carpeta o archivo designado. Tenerlos organizados y accesibles asegura que pueda realizar las pruebas y las citas con especialistas sin demora.

## Pregunta 5

Si su médico ordenó análisis de laboratorio, ¿cuándo debe esperar recibir los resultados?

A) El laboratorio lo llama el mismo día
B) Los médicos generalmente contactan a los pacientes dentro de unos días a una semana con los resultados
C) Nunca recibe noticias a menos que algo esté mal
D) Los resultados se envían por correo a su domicilio en un mes

answer: B
explanation: La mayoría de los consultorios médicos contactan a los pacientes con los resultados de laboratorio dentro de unos días a una semana. Si no ha recibido noticias después de una semana, llame al consultorio. Que no haya noticias no siempre es una buena noticia, por lo que es mejor hacer un seguimiento.

## antibiotic-stewardship

| lessonId  | "antibiotic-stewardship"                        |
| passScore | 70                                              |

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

¿Contra qué tipo de infección son efectivos los antibióticos?

A) La mayoría de resfriados por virus
B) Infecciones bacterianas cuando se recetan apropiadamente
C) Todos los dolores de garganta sin importar la causa
D) Alergias estacionales

answer: B
explanation: Los antibióticos atacan bacterias, no virus ni alergias. La mayoría de resfriados y muchas faringitis son virales; solo causas bacterianas específicas justifican antibióticos tras evaluación adecuada.

## Pregunta 2

¿Por qué preocupa suspender antibióticos antes de tiempo?

A) Siempre causa resistencia instantánea en el paciente
B) Puede no eliminar la infección y seleccionar bacterias más difíciles de tratar
C) Hace que el medicamento funcione mejor después
D) No afecta los resultados del tratamiento

answer: B
explanation: El tratamiento incompleto puede dejar bacterias sobrevivientes y contribuir a resistencia. No causa resistencia permanente instantánea ni mejora la eficacia futura, y sí afecta los resultados.

## Pregunta 3

¿Qué efecto secundario grave se vincula con antibióticos?

A) Colitis por C. difficile
B) Mejor visión
C) Inmunidad permanente a todas las infecciones
D) Colesterol más bajo

answer: A
explanation: Los antibióticos pueden alterar la flora intestinal y permitir proliferación de C. diff con diarrea severa. No mejoran la visión, no dan inmunidad amplia ni bajan el colesterol.

## Pregunta 4

¿Qué hacer con pastillas antibióticas sobrantes?

A) Guardarlas para el próximo resfriado
B) Compartirlas con un familiar con síntomas similares
C) Desecharlas de forma segura según indicación — no autotratarse después
D) Tomar doble dosis para terminar el frasco más rápido

answer: C
explanation: Los sobrantes pueden ser el fármaco, dosis o duración incorrectos para una nueva enfermedad. Guardar, compartir o duplicar dosis sin indicación médica es inseguro.

## Pregunta 5

¿Por qué los CDC enfatizan el uso responsable de antibióticos?

A) Los antibióticos ya no se usan en hospitales
B) Las bacterias resistentes hacen las infecciones más difíciles o imposibles de tratar
C) Los virus se vuelven resistentes a antibióticos
D) Significa evitar toda atención médica

answer: B
explanation: La resistencia limita opciones para infecciones bacterianas graves. Los antibióticos siguen siendo esenciales en hospitales; los virus no se vuelven resistentes a antibióticos — las bacterias sí; el uso responsable promueve el uso apropiado, no evitar la atención.

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

¿Cuál es la diferencia entre la ansiedad normal y un trastorno de ansiedad?

A) No hay diferencia
B) La ansiedad normal es temporal y proporcional a una situación; un trastorno de ansiedad implica una preocupación excesiva y persistente que interfiere con la vida diaria
C) Los trastornos de ansiedad son causados por una mala crianza
D) La ansiedad normal solo ocurre por la noche

answer: B
explanation: Todos se sienten ansiosos a veces. La ansiedad normal es una respuesta natural al estrés y desaparece cuando la situación pasa. Un trastorno de ansiedad implica una preocupación intensa y excesiva que dura meses y dificulta trabajar, dormir o socializar.

## Pregunta 2

¿Qué es un ataque de pánico?

A) Una oleada repentina e intensa de miedo que desencadena reacciones físicas graves incluso cuando no hay peligro real
B) Un sentimiento leve de nerviosismo antes de un examen
C) Un estado crónico de preocupación que dura todo el día
D) Un tipo de reacción alérgica

answer: A
explanation: Los ataques de pánico aparecen repentinamente y pueden incluir corazón acelerado, dolor en el pecho, sudoración, temblores, dificultad para respirar y una sensación de pérdida de control. Muchas personas confunden los ataques de pánico con ataques cardíacos. Por lo general, alcanzan su punto máximo en 10 minutos.

## Pregunta 3

¿Cuál de los siguientes es un síntoma común del trastorno de ansiedad generalizada?

A) Sentirse perfectamente tranquilo en todas las situaciones
B) Preocupación excesiva por cosas cotidianas como el trabajo, la salud o la familia que es difícil de controlar
C) Incapacidad total para sentir miedo
D) Brotes repentinos de risa incontrolable

answer: B
explanation: Las personas con trastorno de ansiedad generalizada se preocupan excesivamente por una variedad de preocupaciones cotidianas. La preocupación es desproporcionada a la situación, difícil de controlar y a menudo va acompañada de inquietud, fatiga, tensión muscular y problemas para dormir.

## Pregunta 4

¿Qué técnica de respiración puede ayudar durante un momento de ansiedad aguda?

A) Contener la respiración el mayor tiempo posible
B) Respirar rápida y superficialmente
C) Respiración lenta y profunda inhalando durante 4 segundos, sosteniendo durante 4 y exhalando durante 4
D) Respirar solo por la boca rápidamente

answer: C
explanation: La respiración lenta y profunda activa el sistema nervioso parasimpático, que ayuda a calmar la respuesta al estrés del cuerpo. La respiración cuadrada (inhalar durante 4, sostener durante 4, exhalar durante 4) es una técnica simple que puede reducir los síntomas de ansiedad en el momento.

## Pregunta 5

¿La ansiedad es tratable?

A) No, la ansiedad es una condena de por vida
B) Sí, los trastornos de ansiedad son altamente tratables con terapia, medicación o ambas
C) Sí, pero solo con medicamentos que tienen efectos secundarios graves
D) No, la ansiedad solo se puede controlar con alcohol

answer: B
explanation: Los trastornos de ansiedad son muy tratables. La terapia cognitivo-conductual es particularmente efectiva. Muchas personas también se benefician de la medicación. Con el tratamiento adecuado, la mayoría de las personas con trastornos de ansiedad pueden controlar sus síntomas y vivir vidas plenas y productivas.

## Pregunta 1

¿Cuál es la razón más importante para informar a su médico sobre todos los medicamentos que está tomando?

A) Para que el médico pueda recetar más del mismo medicamento
B) Para evitar interacciones peligrosas entre medicamentos
C) Para ahorrar dinero en su factura de farmacia
D) Para que el médico pueda contactar a su farmacéutico

answer: B
explanation: Informar a su médico sobre cada medicamento que toma, incluidos los de venta libre y los suplementos, ayuda a prevenir interacciones dañinas. Algunos medicamentos pueden anularse entre sí o combinarse para causar efectos secundarios graves.

## Pregunta 2

¿Qué debería preguntarle a su médico antes de comenzar un nuevo medicamento?

A) De qué color es la pastilla
B) Si hay medicamentos similares más baratos en otros países
C) Para qué sirve el medicamento, cómo tomarlo y qué efectos secundarios esperar
D) Cuánto peso perderá al tomarlo

answer: C
explanation: Antes de comenzar cualquier medicamento nuevo, debe entender su propósito, la dosis y el horario correctos, los posibles efectos secundarios y cualquier restricción de alimentos o actividades. Esto le ayuda a tomar el medicamento de forma segura y eficaz.

## Pregunta 3

¿Qué significa el término "genérico" cuando se refiere a un medicamento?

A) Un medicamento que es menos eficaz que el de marca
B) Un medicamento que no requiere receta médica
C) Una copia de un medicamento de marca que tiene los mismos ingredientes activos
D) Un medicamento que solo está disponible en forma líquida

answer: C
explanation: Los medicamentos genéricos contienen los mismos ingredientes activos que los de marca y deben cumplir con los mismos estándares de seguridad y eficacia de la FDA. Por lo general, son mucho más baratos que las versiones de marca.

## Pregunta 4

Si olvida tomar una dosis de su medicamento, ¿cuál es el enfoque más seguro?

A) Tomar una dosis doble en la próxima hora programada
B) Saltarse la dosis olvidada y no tomarla nunca más
C) Revisar la etiqueta del medicamento o preguntar a su farmacéutico qué hacer
D) Triturar la pastilla y mezclarla con comida

answer: C
explanation: Las instrucciones para dosis olvidadas varían según el medicamento. Algunos deben tomarse tan pronto como lo recuerde, mientras que otros deben omitirse si está cerca de la siguiente dosis. Siempre revise la etiqueta o pregunte a su farmacéutico para estar seguro.

## Pregunta 5

¿Por qué es importante llevar siempre consigo una lista actualizada de sus medicamentos?

A) Para mostrársela a su compañía de seguros
B) Los servicios de emergencia necesitan saber qué medicamentos toma
C) Para demostrar que sigue las órdenes de su médico
D) Para comparar precios en diferentes farmacias

answer: B
explanation: En una emergencia, los paramédicos y los médicos de urgencias necesitan saber exactamente qué medicamentos está tomando para tomar decisiones de tratamiento seguras. Una lista actualizada puede prevenir errores peligrosos.

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

¿Qué es el asma?

A) Una condición donde los pulmones se llenan de líquido
B) Una condición crónica donde las vías respiratorias se inflaman y estrechan, dificultando la respiración
C) Una infección temporal de la garganta
D) Un tipo de reacción alérgica a los alimentos

answer: B
explanation: El asma es una condición pulmonar crónica. Las vías respiratorias se hinchan, producen moco adicional y los músculos alrededor de ellas se tensan. Esto estrecha las vías respiratorias y causa sibilancias, tos, opresión en el pecho y dificultad para respirar.

## Pregunta 2

¿Cuál es un desencadenante común de los síntomas del asma?

A) Beber agua fría
B) Ejercicio, alergias, aire frío o infecciones respiratorias
C) Comer demasiada proteína
D) Exposición a la luz solar

answer: B
explanation: Los desencadenantes del asma varían según la persona, pero comúnmente incluyen polen, ácaros del polvo, caspa de mascotas, moho, aire frío, ejercicio, humo y resfriados o gripe. Identificar y evitar sus desencadenantes personales es una parte clave del manejo del asma.

## Pregunta 3

¿Cuál es la diferencia entre un inhalador de rescate y un inhalador de control?

A) No hay diferencia
B) Los inhaladores de rescate se usan a diario; los inhaladores de control se usan solo en emergencias
C) Los inhaladores de rescate proporcionan alivio rápido durante un ataque de asma; los inhaladores de control reducen la inflamación de las vías respiratorias con el tiempo
D) Los inhaladores de control son solo para niños

answer: C
explanation: Los inhaladores de rescate contienen medicación de acción rápida que relaja los músculos de las vías respiratorias durante un ataque, proporcionando alivio rápido. Los inhaladores de control contienen medicación antiinflamatoria que se toma a diario para prevenir síntomas. Ambos juegan un papel importante en el manejo del asma.

## Pregunta 4

¿Qué debe hacer si su inhalador de rescate no alivia los síntomas del asma?

A) Esperar otra hora e intentar de nuevo
B) Tomar una ducha caliente para abrir las vías respiratorias
C) Buscar ayuda médica de emergencia inmediatamente
D) Beber una gran cantidad de agua

answer: C
explanation: Si su inhalador de rescate no funciona o los síntomas empeoran, busque atención de emergencia de inmediato. Los ataques de asma graves pueden poner en peligro la vida. Los signos de un ataque grave incluyen jadeo, incapacidad para hablar en oraciones completas y labios o uñas azules.

## Pregunta 5

¿Se puede curar el asma?

A) Sí, con la medicación adecuada
B) No, el asma es una condición crónica que se puede controlar pero no curar
C) Sí, pero solo con cirugía
D) Sí, desaparece por sí sola después de la infancia

answer: B
explanation: El asma es una condición crónica sin cura, pero se puede controlar eficazmente. Con el tratamiento adecuado, un plan de acción para el asma y evitando los desencadenantes, la mayoría de las personas con asma pueden llevar vidas activas y plenas sin síntomas frecuentes.

## before-your-visit

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

¿Cuál es la cosa más importante que debe llevar a la cita con su médico?

A) Un bocadillo y una botella de agua
B) Su identificación, tarjeta de seguro y una lista de sus medicamentos actuales
C) Un amigo que pueda llevarlo a casa
D) Su libro favorito para leer en la sala de espera

answer: B
explanation: Llevar su identificación y tarjeta de seguro es esencial para registrarse. Una lista actualizada de medicamentos que incluya dosis y frecuencias ayuda a su médico a tomar decisiones seguras e informadas sobre su atención.

## Pregunta 2

¿Por qué debería escribir sus preguntas antes de una visita al médico?

A) Para impresionar a su médico con lo preparado que está
B) Para no olvidar inquietudes importantes durante la cita
C) Porque el recepcionista recoge sus preguntas al registrarse
D) Para que el médico no tenga que hablar con usted

answer: B
explanation: Las visitas al médico suelen ser cortas y pueden ser abrumadoras. Escribir sus preguntas con anticipación asegura que cubra todo lo que le importa, incluso si se siente nervioso o apurado durante la cita.

## Pregunta 3

¿Qué debe hacer si tiene síntomas nuevos pero su cita es dentro de semanas?

A) Esperar hasta la cita y mencionarlos entonces
B) Llamar al consultorio de su médico para preguntar si debe venir antes
C) Ir a la sala de emergencias por cualquier síntoma nuevo
D) Intentar tratar los síntomas por su cuenta sin consejo médico

answer: B
explanation: Si aparecen síntomas nuevos antes de su cita programada, llame al consultorio de su médico. Ellos pueden indicarle si necesita ser visto antes, hablar con una enfermera o si es seguro esperar. Algunos síntomas requieren atención inmediata.

## Pregunta 4

¿Con cuánta anticipación debe llegar para una cita médica típica?

A) 2 a 3 horas antes
B) Exactamente a la hora de la cita, no antes
C) 10 a 15 minutos antes para completar el papeleo
D) Cuando quiera, siempre que llegue antes de que cierre la oficina

answer: C
explanation: Llegar 10 a 15 minutos antes le da tiempo para registrarse, actualizar su información de seguro y completar los formularios necesarios. Esto ayuda a que la cita comience a tiempo y reduce el estrés.

## Pregunta 5

¿Qué es un "resumen de la visita" y por qué es importante?

A) Un resumen de lo que vio en la televisión en la sala de espera
B) Un documento que su médico le entrega y que explica la visita, los nuevos medicamentos y los pasos de seguimiento
C) Una factura de la cita
D) Un resumen que su amigo escribe sobre sus síntomas

answer: B
explanation: Un resumen de la visita es un documento que describe lo que se discutió durante su cita, incluidos diagnósticos, cambios de medicación e instrucciones de seguimiento. Revisarlo ayuda a asegurarse de que entiende y recuerda su plan de cuidado.

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

¿Cuáles son los componentes principales de la sangre?

A) Agua, sal y azúcar
B) Glóbulos rojos, glóbulos blancos, plaquetas y plasma
C) Oxígeno, dióxido de carbono y nitrógeno
D) Vitaminas, minerales y proteínas

answer: B
explanation: La sangre está compuesta por cuatro componentes principales. Los glóbulos rojos transportan oxígeno, los glóbulos blancos combaten infecciones, las plaquetas ayudan con la coagulación y el plasma es el líquido que los transporta a todos. Cada uno juega un papel vital para mantenerlo saludable.

## Pregunta 2

¿Cuál es la función principal de los glóbulos rojos?

A) Combatir infecciones
B) Transportar oxígeno desde los pulmones al resto del cuerpo
C) Ayudar a que la sangre coagule después de una lesión
D) Digerir los alimentos en el estómago

answer: B
explanation: Los glóbulos rojos contienen hemoglobina, una proteína que recoge oxígeno en sus pulmones y lo entrega a los tejidos de todo su cuerpo. Los recuentos bajos de glóbulos rojos pueden causar fatiga y debilidad, una condición llamada anemia.

## Pregunta 3

¿Qué hacen los glóbulos blancos?

A) Ayudan a respirar
B) Transportan nutrientes a sus órganos
C) Combaten infecciones y protegen contra enfermedades
D) Controlan la temperatura de su cuerpo

answer: C
explanation: Los glóbulos blancos son parte de su sistema inmunológico. Identifican y atacan gérmenes como bacterias y virus. Un recuento alto de glóbulos blancos puede indicar que su cuerpo está combatiendo una infección.

## Pregunta 4

¿Cuál es el papel de las plaquetas en la sangre?

A) Transportar oxígeno al cerebro
B) Combatir virus
C) Ayudar a que la sangre coagule para detener el sangrado
D) Transportar hormonas

answer: C
explanation: Las plaquetas son pequeños fragmentos celulares que se agrupan en el sitio de una lesión para formar un tapón y detener el sangrado. Sin suficientes plaquetas, incluso los cortes pequeños pueden sangrar excesivamente.

## Pregunta 5

¿Qué es el plasma?

A) La parte sólida de la sangre
B) La parte líquida de la sangre que transporta células, nutrientes y desechos
C) Un tipo de glóbulo blanco
D) Una proteína que ayuda con la digestión

answer: B
explanation: El plasma es la porción líquida de la sangre, que constituye aproximadamente el 55 por ciento del volumen sanguíneo total. Transporta células sanguíneas, nutrientes, hormonas y productos de desecho por todo el cuerpo. El plasma es principalmente agua pero contiene proteínas y electrolitos importantes.

## building-balanced-plate

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

Según el modelo MiPlato, ¿qué porciones de su plato deben llenarse con frutas y verduras?

A) Un cuarto
B) Aproximadamente la mitad del plato
C) El plato entero
D) Una pequeña esquina del plato

answer: B
explanation: El modelo MiPlato recomienda llenar la mitad de su plato con frutas y verduras. Estos alimentos son ricos en vitaminas, minerales y fibra, y bajos en calorías. Comer una variedad de productos coloridos asegura que obtenga una gama de nutrientes.

## Pregunta 2

¿Qué tipo de granos deben constituir al menos la mitad de los granos que consume?

A) Granos refinados blancos como pan blanco y arroz blanco
B) Granos integrales como trigo integral, arroz integral, avena y quinua
C) Solo granos enriquecidos
D) Postres a base de granos como galletas y pasteles

answer: B
explanation: Los granos integrales contienen el grano entero, proporcionando más fibra, proteína, vitaminas y minerales que los granos refinados. La fibra ayuda con la digestión, lo mantiene satisfecho por más tiempo y puede reducir el colesterol y los niveles de azúcar en sangre.

## Pregunta 3

¿Cuál es una fuente saludable de proteína para incluir en su plato?

A) Pollo frito y tocino
B) Carne magra, aves, pescado, frijoles, huevos, nueces y tofu
C) Embutidos procesados
D) Alimentos fritos en aceite

answer: B
explanation: Las fuentes saludables de proteína incluyen carnes magras, pescado, aves, huevos, frijoles, lentejas, tofu, nueces y semillas. Estas proporcionan aminoácidos esenciales sin exceso de grasa saturada. Trate de incluir una variedad de fuentes de proteína durante la semana.

## Pregunta 4

¿Qué tipo de grasa se considera saludable para el corazón?

A) Grasas saturadas que se encuentran en la mantequilla y la carne roja
B) Grasas trans que se encuentran en muchos bocadillos procesados
C) Grasas insaturadas que se encuentran en el aceite de oliva, aguacates, nueces y pescado
D) Todas las grasas son igualmente saludables

answer: C
explanation: Las grasas insaturadas, incluidas las monoinsaturadas y poliinsaturadas, pueden ayudar a mejorar los niveles de colesterol y reducir el riesgo de enfermedades cardíacas. Las fuentes incluyen aceite de oliva, aguacates, nueces, semillas y pescados grasos como el salmón. Limite las saturadas y evite las grasas trans.

## Pregunta 5

¿Qué debería beber con una comida equilibrada para la opción más saludable?

A) Refresco azucarado o té endulzado
B) Agua o bebidas sin endulzar
C) Bebidas energéticas
D) Ponche de frutas con azúcar añadido

answer: B
explanation: El agua es la opción más saludable para acompañar cualquier comida. Hidrata sin añadir calorías ni azúcar. Las bebidas azucaradas son una fuente importante de azúcar añadido y calorías vacías. El té sin endulzar o la leche también son buenas opciones.

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

¿Cuál de los siguientes es un elemento esencial para un botiquín básico de primeros auxilios?

A) Un kit de costura
B) Vendas adhesivas en tamaños variados
C) Una botella de refresco
D) Una revista

answer: B
explanation: Las vendas adhesivas son uno de los elementos más básicos y esenciales de primeros auxilios. Un botiquín bien surtido debe incluir varios tamaños para cortes, raspaduras y ampollas. Protegen las heridas de la suciedad y las bacterias mientras cicatrizan.

## Pregunta 2

¿Cuál es el propósito de incluir toallitas antisépticas en un botiquín de primeros auxilios?

A) Limpiarse las manos antes de comer
B) Limpiar la piel alrededor de una herida para prevenir infecciones
C) Limpiar líquidos derramados
D) Quitarse el maquillaje

answer: B
explanation: Las toallitas antisépticas matan los gérmenes en la piel alrededor de una herida, reduciendo el riesgo de infección. Limpie la herida suavemente antes de aplicar una venda. No use alcohol directamente dentro de heridas profundas, ya que puede dañar el tejido.

## Pregunta 3

¿Por qué debería incluir una mascarilla o escudo facial de RCP en su botiquín de primeros auxilios?

A) Para protegerse del sol
B) Para realizar respiraciones de rescate de forma segura sin contacto directo boca a boca
C) Para cubrirse la cara durante el clima frío
D) Para filtrar el polvo del aire

answer: B
explanation: Una mascarilla o escudo facial de RCP crea una barrera al realizar respiraciones de rescate, reduciendo el riesgo de transmisión de enfermedades. Es un artículo pequeño y económico que hace que los espectadores estén más dispuestos a realizar RCP en una emergencia.

## Pregunta 4

¿Con qué frecuencia debe revisar y reabastecer su botiquín de primeros auxilios?

A) Una vez cada 10 años
B) Cada pocos meses para reemplazar artículos caducados y reabastecer suministros usados
C) Nunca, una vez que está surtido dura para siempre
D) Solo después de usarlo para una emergencia mayor

answer: B
explanation: Revise su botiquín de primeros auxilios cada pocos meses. Reemplace los medicamentos caducados, reabastezca las vendas y toallitas usadas, y asegúrese de que las baterías de la linterna funcionen. Un botiquín desactualizado o con suministros faltantes no es útil en una emergencia.

## Pregunta 5

¿Cuál es el mejor lugar para guardar un botiquín de primeros auxilios en su hogar?

A) En una caja fuerte que solo los adultos puedan abrir
B) En un lugar de fácil acceso que todos en el hogar conozcan
C) En el garaje detrás de cajas
D) En un gabinete alto que requiera un banco para alcanzar

answer: B
explanation: Su botiquín de primeros auxilios debe ser fácil de alcanzar en una emergencia. Colóquelo en un lugar central y accesible y asegúrese de que todos los miembros del hogar sepan dónde está. Evite cerrarlo con llave, ya que los segundos importan durante una lesión.

### Quiz Content

## Pregunta 1

¿Propósito principal de la detección?

A) Diagnosticar cada síntoma
B) Encontrar signos tempranos antes de síntomas
C) Reemplazar tratamiento
D) Garantizar que nunca habrá cáncer

answer: B
explanation: Las pruebas de detección buscan cáncer temprano o cambios precancerosos antes de sentirse enfermo. No diagnostican cada síntoma — son herramientas preventivas para edades y niveles de riesgo recomendados.

## Pregunta 2

¿Edad típica de inicio para colon en guías de EE.UU.?

A) 18
B) 45
C) 70
D) Solo con síntomas

answer: B
explanation: Las guías de EE.UU. recomiendan detección de cáncer colorrectal desde los 45 años en adultos de riesgo promedio. Puede necesitarse antes con historial familiar. Los 18 o 70 solos no son edades estándar de inicio.

## Pregunta 3

¿Por qué importa el historial familiar?

A) Nunca cambia recomendaciones
B) Puede llevar a detección antes o más frecuente
C) El médico ya lo sabe
D) Solo en niños

answer: B
explanation: Un padre o hermano con ciertos cánceres puede aumentar su riesgo. Los médicos pueden recomendar mamografías o colonoscopia antes o con más frecuencia. No pueden asumir su historial sin que usted lo comparta.

## Pregunta 4

¿Qué hacer si el resultado es anormal?

A) Ignorarlo
B) Preguntar qué significa y siguientes pasos
C) Dejar toda detección
D) Autotratarse

answer: B
explanation: Un resultado anormal no siempre significa cáncer, pero requiere seguimiento. Pregunte qué significa, qué prueba sigue y cuándo. Ignorar resultados o dejar toda detección es inseguro.

## Pregunta 5

¿Puede la detección no ver cáncer?

A) No — 100% exacta
B) Sí — reporte síntomas nuevos tras resultado normal
C) Solo en jóvenes
D) Solo cáncer de piel

answer: B
explanation: Ninguna prueba detecta todo el cáncer. Hay falsos negativos. Si tiene síntomas nuevos — sangrado, bultos, dolor persistente — repórtelos aunque una prueba reciente fue normal.
